- 🟡 macOS rendering performance, part 1 (contribution by LisaScheers in PR #1473, split by the maintainers on 2026-10-30 at the human's request; task `macos-render-scale`; render scale validated by the human in demo on Windows on 2026-10-30, unchanged at 100 %; follows the base port merged in #1463): use the binding-array limit for texture pages (the ordinary sampled-texture limit incorrectly capped Metal at 79 pages); add a 50–100% world render scale with Catmull-Rom spatial upscaling, native UI/HUDs and full-resolution snapshots. - 🟡 The poser poses avatars whose shape mirrors a joint ([#1249](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/issues/1249); task `poser-not-posing`, 2026-10-29; validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-29): shape sliders at their ends give some face and pectoral joints a negative scale on one axis (Head Shape at 100 does it to the forehead; LLPolySkeletalDistortion adds scale deltas without a floor), and the poser refused the whole pose of such an avatar: it neither froze nor moved, with no Start button. Joint scales are now checked by size and keep their sign; a mirrored joint is read with the axis whose local rotation is nearest the rig's rest one (a matrix does not tell which axis is mirrored), so that a preset, a pose file or the T-pose does not turn it over; scale edits keep the sign. Demo: `AURORA_DEMO_POSER=square-head`.
  - ⬜ Grid check: the reporter's own shape (or Head Shape at 100) freezes and takes the pose.

- 🟡 Poser close confirmation and Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y (human request, 2026-10-29; task `poser-close-undo`; no issue; follows #1450; validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-29): with stop on close, a close that loses edited joints (any subject) asks first: Minimize keeps the pose, Close anyway closes, Escape cancels, Don't ask again turns off the new Settings › Window switch (on by default). The Legacy Viewer closes at once (`FSFloaterPoser::onClose`); asking avoids losing a pose by mistake. Covers the cross, Ctrl+W and the photo viewfinder's wand; Stop posing only pauses and does not ask. Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y and Ctrl+Shift+Z undo and redo in the poser as its title arrows (an Aurora addition: the Legacy poser has buttons only), unless a text field has the keyboard or the build tools' window is in front; gestures bound to them wait while the poser is open. Ctrl+W now finds a window raised over the viewfinder. The demo simulator answers the build tools' Undo / Redo (placements per object, one step per drag). Demo: `AURORA_DEMO_POSER=close`.
  - ⬜ Grid check: the build tools' Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y on a real simulator after moving, rotating and stretching an object.

- 🟡 PBR terrain surfaces and live editing ([#1221](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/issues/1221); [draft PR #1255](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/pull/1255); human follow-up, 2026-10-28; task `region-terrain-pbr`): render the four material layers and their colour, normal, ORM and emissive maps, with the Legacy Viewer's triplanar projection, layer thresholds and 8 m defaults. GPU material swatches show all four selections; texture/material picker changes preview locally before OK or Apply, and Cancel beside the swatches restores only the cover. Picker cancellation restores its opening selection; closing or losing management permissions removes the local preview. Only Apply sends a simulator edit. Blank materials have a known local appearance; terrain pickers reject None. English/French controls reuse existing translations. This extends the initial picker fix in `8e959483`.

No rendering errors in those capture logs. All capped at 60 fps; opaque GPU frame 2.85 ms (previous reference 2.52-2.55 ms), scene sync 0.06 ms, no terrain rebuild or vertex upload while stationary. Corrected the GL-to-top-down image conversion, 512 px terrain decode request (now the reference 2048 px priority), default diagonal normal stencil, and mesh-accumulated tangents. Existing parallel vertex bytes retain snorm16 direction precision, while composition and transition noise use floats. Tangent transforms run per vertex; interpolated tangents and terrain ORM roughness follow the reference shader. Height/noise transitions now use the actual 256-square 2D alpha ramp instead of the former 1D approximation, with matching local bake weights. GPU regressions include asymmetric JPEG2000 base/normal assets, curved frames and independent bilinear ramp samples; `manage:pbr-slopes` adds a sharp mound and hollow. Full `scripts/check.ps1` green: 5,960 passed, zero failures, 30 ignored; formatting, scripts and Clippy clean. Dev viewer `0.8.1+9.g5aa21611e` built. Five native scenarios and the unobstructed curved-terrain photo inspected: opaque ground, mound/hollow, selection before OK, masked holes and local paintmap. No rendering errors in their logs; all capped at 60 fps. Opaque GPU frame 2.88 ms (previous iteration 2.85 ms), curved terrain 3.56 ms, other scenarios 2.87-3.09 ms; sync 0.06-0.09 ms, no stationary terrain rebuild or vertex upload. These shared-desktop timings are not an isolated benchmark. Local review completed without remaining findings. New human comparison on the same terrain is required before claiming visual parity or resolving #1221.
  - Draft PR validation: full post-rebase `scripts/check.ps1` green (5,971 passed, zero failures, 30 ignored); scripts, formatting and Clippy clean. Terrain GPU shader extraction accepts both LF and CRLF source files. Human visual comparison remains pending.
  - ✅ Validated by the human on Agni on 2026-10-28: a region with PBR terrain materials, side by side with the Legacy Viewer (same materials, repeats and relief; the gray ground of #1221 is gone). Textured terrain checked by the human on a mainland region the same day (looks right), and in demo against main.
  - ✅ Taken over on 2026-10-28 (handed over by its author): rebased on main. Region transform overrides are merged field by field as LLGLTFMaterial::applyOverride does (a rotation alone keeps the material's scale and offset); the mask cutoff is divided by the base colour alpha as renderFullShaderPBR does. Terrain shadow casters have their own pipeline (`shadow_terrain`: `vs_shadow_terrain` / `fs_shadow_terrain`, unless drawn depth only), so `vs_shadow` / `fs_shadow` are main's again for every other caster (no terrain varyings or derivatives on foliage and projector shadows). The unused `FLAG_UNLIT_SHADOWLESS` (same bit as `FLAG_TERRAIN`) is removed; a second seed answer asks ModifyRegion only when it brings that capability. Visible on every region, textured ones included: the diagonal normal stencil (LLSurfacePatch::calcNormal<false>) and the 2048 px terrain texture priority, to compare on a textured region as well as a PBR one.
    - Classic and PBR terrain now have their own shaders and pipelines (`vs_terrain` / `fs_terrain` as on main for textured regions; `vs_terrain_pbr` / `fs_terrain_pbr` and their depth, pick, reflection and shadow variants for PBR ones; draw lists `terrain`, `terrain_pbr`, `terrain_mask`, `reflection_terrain_pbr`). Measured in the classic demo (`AURORA_PROFILE=1`, median of 15 s, shared desktop): `g_terrain_sky` 0.113 ms on main, 0.251 ms with the single terrain shader, 0.131 ms after the split; GPU frame 0.79 / 1.03 / 0.84 ms. Classic terrain captures on main and on the branch look the same.
  - ⬜ Human grid validation: see existing PBR terrain with Region / Estate closed, select materials or classic textures and see each swatch and the ground update before Apply; cancel the picker and the cover; Apply and confirm persistence in the Legacy Viewer. Test material transforms and both region window styles.
  - Rendering parity follow-up under human comparison: masked terrain enters the sun/projector alpha shadow passes and uses the same production mask as camera depth. Terrain KHR rotation and triplanar normal orientation follow `pbrterrainUtilF.glsl` / `textureUtilV.glsl`. The advanced terrain fold includes the Legacy Viewer's experimental local paintmap bake/reset (2048 px, 1024 on small upload pools; background composition and staging, linear RGB/remainder weights, mip-aware edge clamping, no estate publication). Frozen weights survive scene recreation without retaining staging chunks. Region terrain is still transmitted as height/noise composition; paintmaps in the reference sources are a local experiment. Both region window styles expose the local controls; resetting a map restores live composition without sending an edit.

- 🟡 Limit select distance and limit drag distance (human request, 2026-10-27; task `select-distance`; no matching open issue; merged at the human's request before their test, a test viewer left open for them): the Legacy Viewer's LimitSelectDistance / MaxSelectDistance and LimitDragDistance / MaxDragDistance (settings.xml; Build 1 preferences, 0.001 to 1024 m) become build settings, in a new "Distance limits" section of the construction settings under the ruler. The select limit governs every place the 128 m constant did: automatic deselection when the avatar walks away (LLSelectMgr::updateSelectionCenter), rectangle selection (llglsandbox.cpp), the edit stack under the cursor, the create and copy-selection tools and their preview (LLToolPlacer::raycastForNewObjPos), and the manipulator handles (LLManipTranslate / Rotate / Scale). The drag limit stops one move past its distance (LLManipTranslate::handleHover). Difference, at the human's request: LimitSelectDistance is off by default (the Legacy Viewer has it on at 128 m), so nothing is out of reach; the drag limit keeps the Legacy default (on, 48 m). Without the limit, the create tool's simulator ray reaches past a surface farther than the Legacy Viewer's 129 m. The Legacy Viewer's Advanced menu toggle has no place here: Aurora has no such menu. Full `scripts/check.ps1` green: 4,961 + 405 + 282 passed, zero failures; fmt, scripts and Clippy clean. Tests: far selection kept while unlimited and deselected past the set distance, range and defaults of both limits, edit stack under the cursor with and without the limit. French demo capture of the construction settings inspected.
  - ⬜ To verify (human): select, move and create past 128 m with the limit off; switch it on at a short distance and walk away from a selection.
- 🟡 Unlink keeps every prim selected, and a rectangle drawn from a skybox leaves the ground out (tester report on X after 0.8.4, 2026-10-31; task `unlink-and-skybox-select`; no matching open issue; [PR #1747](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/pull/1747); validated by the human in demo mode on 2026-10-31). Unlink: Aurora selects linkset roots only, so after an unlink only the former root stayed selected; each former prim now joins the selection once the simulator makes it a root, the former root first, like the Legacy Viewer's per-prim LLSelectNodes after LLSelectMgr::sendDelink. A selection changed before the reply is left alone. Rectangle selection: LimitSelectDistance is on by default again, like the Legacy Viewer (128 m from the avatar, llglsandbox.cpp handleRectangleSelection); off, a rectangle around a skybox seen from above took other residents' objects far below, so Lock and other bulk actions refused the selection. Settings version 30 turns it on once for files that wrote the former default; switching it off afterwards is kept. This reverses the "off by default" choice of the `select-distance` task above. Full `scripts/check.ps1` green: 5,499 viewer tests passed, zero failures; fmt, scripts and Clippy clean. Tests: every former prim selected after the simulator's reply, a selection changed before the reply left alone, the settings migration and the new defaults.
  - ⬜ To verify (human, grid): a rectangle around a skybox seen from above selects the skybox only and Lock applies; unlinking a real linkset keeps every prim selected.
- 🟡 Select only my objects / Select only movable objects (feedback board post 130, human request, 2026-10-30; task `select-owned-only`; no matching open issue; validated by the human in demo mode on 2026-10-30): the Legacy Viewer's SelectOwnedOnly and SelectMovableOnly (settings.xml, off by default, kept between sessions; LLSelectMgr::canSelectObject) become two construction settings right under "Select reflection probes", organizable and exported to notecards like the other options. They filter clicks in the edit, face, align and create tools, rectangle selection, the edit stack under the cursor and Area Search's selection; ownership and the move right are read on the linkset root (permYouOwner / permMove), and a permanent pathfinding object only counts as movable in the agent's region (isPermanentEnforced). The right-click menu's temporary selection ignores them, like the Legacy Viewer's temp_select. Difference: the Legacy Viewer has them in its Build › Options menu; Aurora has no such menu, so they live in the construction settings. In the Legacy-style build window they head its settings panel, as the window's fixed checkbox block has no room under the probes. Full `scripts/check.ps1` green: 5,459 viewer tests passed, zero failures; fmt, scripts and Clippy clean. Tests: clicks, Shift, Area Search, the wheel, rectangles and the right-click menu with the filter on; root rights and permanent objects; persistence, notecards and the position of the options in an older saved layout.
  - ⬜ To verify on the grid (human): with "Select only my objects" on, a click and a rectangle in a store or a sandbox select only our own objects; with "Select only movable objects" on, a no-move object (a store's display, a region's permanent object) cannot be selected.
  - ⬜ Later: the Legacy Viewer's other selection filters (Select only locked objects, Select only copyable objects, Include group-owned objects).
- 🟡 Select by surrounding (#1680, PR #1691; task `select-by-surrounding`, follows #1685; validated by the human in demo mode on 2026-10-30): the Legacy Viewer's RectangleSelectInclusive ("Select By Surrounding", on by default, kept between sessions) becomes a construction setting right under "Select only movable objects", organizable and exported to notecards (absent from an older notecard: on). The selection rectangle follows LLToolSelectRect::handleRectangleSelection: every prim is tested, children included, and outside linked editing brings its linkset; a prim's box wholly inside or outside the rectangle decides at once, one across an edge is decided by its drawn vertices (LLViewerCamera::areVertsVisible): all of them inside with the option on, one is enough with it off. Before, Aurora took a linkset when its root's center was inside, which matched neither mode. Tests: box and vertex rules, the option on a real rectangle, persistence and older notecards.
  - ⬜ To verify on the grid (human): in a busy region or a sandbox, a rectangle that only partly covers an object leaves it out with the option on and takes it with the option off; a large mesh (a house, a skybox wall) behaves the same.
- 🟡 Own avatar missing some outfit attachments after a login, Replace outfit not putting them back (task `outfit-attachments`, 2026-10-27; found during the cold-cache arrival measurements, the Legacy Viewer loses objects the same way now and then): at login the region puts back by itself one object per attachment point; the objects added on top are the viewer's to request (LLAppearanceMgr::updateAppearanceFromCOF, ATTACHMENT_ADD). Aurora requested them about 5 s after arriving, while the region was still putting its own back, all in one burst: "Attempt to rez an object failed" and, on a busy region, 18 of 38 objects missing with exactly one left per point. `world/outfit.rs` now waits for the region's restore to be quiet (4 s without a change, 12 s if nothing comes, 30 s at most), asks for the rest, asks again at once for an object the region takes off (its COF link kept, unlike a detach asked by the resident), and logs every step with item names; `session/attach_queue.rs` sends one RezMultipleAttachmentsFromInv at a time (LLAttachmentsMgr::requestAttachments), a limited number waiting for their object (8 at first, one more every 4 objects arrived up to 12, halved by a refusal, which also pauses it 5 s; four at a time made an outfit change on a busy region take two minutes), with a log line per run: on the grid, 18 requests 20 ms apart got the last 4 refused, and a refused item then stayed off for the session. Replace outfit keeps the Aurora bridge, as the Legacy Viewer puts it back into a replaced outfit. The COF sync after Replace outfit / Add no longer takes off a worn object whose link it cannot resolve yet and wears the objects it could not resolve once FetchItems brings them. Visible difference: the added objects appear a few seconds later than in the Legacy Viewer. Demo: `AURORA_DEMO_OUTFIT_RESTORE=warm|cold`.
  - Validated by the human on AGNI on 2026-10-27, warm cache, crowded region: login 37 of 37 worn (the region put back 17 by itself, 20 requested, worn in 12 s), three outfit changes with no alert (22 objects worn in 6.5 s, 27 in 4.6 s), the Aurora bridge kept.
  - ⬜ To verify on the grid (human): a cold inventory cache login, launched outside Claude.

- 🟡 Freeze the world in photo mode ([#1154](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/issues/1154); task `photo-freeze-world`, 2026-10-27; validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-27): a snowflake in the viewfinder's dock (fifth above the shutter), a "Freeze the world" tile in the quick menu (after Freeze frame) and a switch in the photo panel (under Freeze frame) hold every avatar, animation and moving thing still while the camera flies on; "World frozen" shows in the Full display. Rule from LLFloater360Capture::freezeWorld and the FreezeTime setting (indra/newview/llfloater360capture.cpp, pipeline.cpp, llviewerobjectlist.cpp): every character paused (LLCharacter::requestPause, here `Scene::pause_all_skeletons`, the motions resuming where they stopped), objects not moved (LLPipeline::updateMove), particles and clouds stopped. Aurora reuses the tiled photo's held instant (`snapshot::Hold`) for animations, avatar physics, flexible prims, water and portals, holds the animated textures' GPU clock too (`FrameParams::tex_anim_at`, the frame uniform's `anim_clock.zw`; now also held for photos in tiles), while the rez effects and the avatars' loading clouds go on, so what the moving camera finds still rezzes in, and keeps the objects that move, or that a report would move, at the place they were drawn (`ObjectStore::hold_poses`), our own avatar included; reports are still applied, so the world is current again on thaw. Never saved: leaving the photo mode thaws it. Demo word `frozen` (`AURORA_DEMO_SNAPSHOT=viewfinder-frozen`): captures at frames 700 and 900 differ by no pixel outside the hint banner (5,110 sampled pixels without the freeze).
  - Grid test by the QA on 2026-10-29: avatars, animated objects, moving objects, vehicles and walking avatars hold ✅; particle scripts still started new particles and derezzed objects still vanished ❌.
  - 🟡 Fix (task `freeze-world-holds`, 2026-10-29; checked in demo with captures, `scripts/check.ps1` green; PR opened at the human's request, validation handed to the QA team): while frozen no object's particle source emits, a script's new or restarted system included (LLViewerPartSim::enable(false), whose zero particle count makes shouldAddPart refuse every particle); before, a source born under the frozen clock burst at every frame (LL's first run never ended). The avatars' loading clouds keep the live clock, like the rez effects. What the simulator kills while frozen stays drawn until the thaw (`World::hold_kills`), then goes unless its key went to another object meanwhile; what the user does goes at once (an attachment of our avatar taken off, an object we own). A visible difference from the Legacy Viewer, whose FreezeTime still removes them, asked for by the QA. Demo `AURORA_DEMO_FREEZE_WORLD=1` with `AURORA_DEMO_SNAPSHOT=viewfinder-frozen`.
  - ⬜ To verify on the grid: avatars walking and dancing, a moving vehicle, objects and avatars arriving while frozen, a photo in tiles while frozen; a particle script started or changed while frozen, an object derezzed and an avatar leaving while frozen, gone on thaw.
  - ⬜ Later: a viewfinder key for the freeze; the sky's day cycle (wall clock) and the portal swirl are not held.

- 🟡 Mesh import preview ignores BLEND ([#1157](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/issues/1157); [PR #1217](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/pull/1217); task `mesh-preview-ignore-blend`, 2026-10-27; validated by the human in the online test viewer): the Legacy Viewer's model preview draws with depth writes and blending disabled, while Aurora sent a glTF BLEND surface to a pass without depth writes even when its texture was fully opaque. The mesh import preview now draws BLEND surfaces as opaque, so their depth occludes later surfaces; the source material, material preview and Mask mode stay unchanged. Confirmation from the reporter remains pending; the original file's export format and alpha mode were not available for this investigation.
- 🟡 Rigged mesh layers z-fight in the upload preview ([#1157](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/issues/1157); [PR #1159](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/pull/1159); task `mesh-preview-layers`, 2026-10-27; validation handed to QA by the human): a mesh body whose layers share their positions (onion skins) showed a diamond z-fighting pattern in the rigged preview, clean in the Legacy Viewer. The Legacy Viewer keys skin weights by position (LLDAELoader / LLGLTFLoader `mSkinWeights[position]`, the last vertex written at a position wins; LLModel::getJointInfluences returns the first position in LLVector3 order within 1e-5 in normalized space), so coincident vertices of different layers skin identically; Aurora kept each source vertex's own list, and slightly different weights moved the layers apart by rounding. `skin::share_weights` now applies that rule in both loaders before `complete_weights`, which also fixes the weights sent at upload. Regressions `mesh_import_parity_dae_coincident_layers_share_the_last_source_weights` and `mesh_import_parity_near_positions_take_the_first_weights_within_epsilon`. A position grid (cells of twice the tolerance) and a parallel vertex pass keep it to about 130 ms for 600,000 vertices (dev build), once per load on the import worker. Synthetic demo check (`AURORA_DEMO_IMPORTS=mesh` with `AURORA_DEMO_IMPORT_FILE` on a red/blue two-layer rigged tube whose weights differ by 1e-4): before, red patches through the blue layer; after, a clean blue layer.
  - 🟡 QA: import a rigged layered mesh body (the reporter's case) with weights shown; the preview must match the Legacy Viewer's, with no diamond pattern between layers, and the uploaded body worn in-world must look the same.

- 🟡 A resident typing to us shows on their picture ([#1233](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/issues/1233); task `typing-thumbnails`, 2026-10-28; validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-28): in the Conversations list (column and rail) and on the conversation thumbnails, the name plates' three bouncing dots on a pill across the bottom of the picture, in place of the status dot, while they type (IM_TYPING_START, until their stop, their message or OTHER_TYPING_TIMEOUT). Private conversations only: a group's session carries no typing. An Aurora addition (the Legacy Viewer says it in the tab only), `ui/chat/sidebar.rs` (`paint_typing`). Demo: `AURORA_DEMO_CONV=aurora` (the friend types) with `AURORA_DEMO_THUMBNAILS=bar`.
  - ⬜ To verify on Agni: another resident typing an IM to us shows the dots on their entry and thumbnail, gone when they stop, send or after nine seconds.

- 🟡 Photo freezes the viewer when the card is over its memory budget ([#1529](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/issues/1529), [#1536](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/issues/1536), duplicate [#1531](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/issues/1531), [PR #1664](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/pull/1664); task `photo-tile-floor`, 2026-10-30; validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-30): the pixels of a photo pass came from half the video memory left under the driver's budget; in a busy region the textures push the card over it, nothing was left, and the photo was drawn in passes of 32 x 32 pixels (about 16 x 16 kept with the guard band): thousands of frames with the world held still, the viewer stuck for minutes (three crash reports, 0.8.2, killed from the Task Manager). A pass now draws at least the window's pixels (`snapshot::pass_pixels`), as LLViewerWindow::rawSnapshot falls back to tiles of the window's size: a 2x photo of a 1318 x 745 window takes a few passes. Demo with `AURORA_VRAM_BUDGET_MB=256`: a 1280 x 720 photo took 3,600 passes and 26.6 s before, 1 pass and 52 ms after; 7680 x 4320 takes 12 passes, 574 ms, no seam.
  - ⬜ To verify on the grid: in a busy region with the textures under pressure, a photo at the window's size, 4K with the photo quality and 8K: each finishes in a few seconds at most.
- 🟡 Photo quality loses the GPU when video memory is tight (Refs [#1374](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/issues/1374); task `photo-vram-budget`, 2026-10-31; merged without a human test at the human's request, grid check left: a card short of video memory): the photo quality raised every setting at once (MSAA 8x at the window's size, 512 m, shadows 4…, about 1.4 GB more at 3440 x 1369) whatever the memory left; after hours in a busy region the driver's budget had fallen to 5,280 MB with 4,431 MB taken and the textures at pressure 6 / 7, and the GPU was lost 1.4 s after the switch. It now lowers itself to fit (`snapshot::quality::plan`, unit-tested): steps from the whole boost to the user's own settings, the MSAA first (8x, 4x, 2x, the user's anti-aliasing), then the draw distance (384, 256, 128 m, the user's), then the shadows (level 3, the user's), then everything else; the first step whose estimated cost (render targets × samples, shadow atlas, about 512 bytes per m² of ground from a KB measurement, reflections, probes) fits under the budget less a tenth of it (at least 512 MB) and up to a tenth more with the texture pressure. Read again every second while the window is open: down at once, up one step at a time after 5 s and with a twentieth of the budget (at least 256 MB) to spare; never while a photo is drawn; a setting the user changes meanwhile stays theirs; the textures in view are forced to full resolution only with the whole boost. The panel shows "Quality reduced: video memory almost full" under Resolution, the viewfinder says it once at the top. Without figures from the driver, or with room to spare, nothing changes. Demo: `AURORA_DEMO_SNAPSHOT=quality-tight[:<MB>[:<MB later>]]`.
  - ⬜ Human validation in demo, then on the grid: a busy region with the textures under pressure, on a card with 8 GB or less; the photo quality on: the line shows, the log gives `photo quality: step <k> of <n> for the video memory`, no GPU lost.
- 🟡 Large photos come out black, or lose the GPU, on slower cards (Refs [#1649](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/issues/1649), [#1374](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/issues/1374); residents' reports of all-black photos, 2026-10-31; task `photo-gpu-timeout`; validated by the human in demo on the Radeon on 2026-10-31, in their own window and settings: 4K in 1 pass, 8K in 6, 8K with the photo quality in 6, no ring timeout; retested after the review's fixes the same day: 4582 x 7680 photos with and without the Cinema 2.39:1 look all saved, a part black under the look's bars drawn again in 35 parts of the window's size, 9 s instead of 5): a photo the video memory holds was drawn in one pass, however long the GPU took. A driver ends a job past about two seconds (Windows' TDR; Linux's amdgpu resets the ring): the pass read back black and was saved as the photo, or the device was lost and the viewer closed. Reproduced in demo on a Radeon 610M (RADV): every photo of 7040 x 3960 or more in one pass was black (2.67 s; 6400 x 3600 in 2.46 s went through), one with the anti-aliasing off lost the device; the kernel logged a ring timeout for each. A pass now also stays within 500 ms of GPU time (`snapshot::GpuCost`, unit-tested): the renderer reports the pixels its GPU time measures (`RenderStats::gpu_pixels`), the slowest recent cost of a pixel (frames of 1 Mpx or more, falling by 1 % a frame) bounds the pass, never below the window's frame; 4K at most without GPU timers; a photo with the interface or the HUDs, which a photo in parts leaves out, may take 1500 ms a pass (`OVERLAY_PASS_GPU_MS`). A pass that still reads back black (`snapshot::blank`: the colour of every pixel; the black pass's alpha stays opaque; cut-out photos not checked) is drawn again from the start in passes of a quarter of its pixels at most, for the rest of the photo, down to the window's frame, where a black part is kept (a dark scene, a look's bars); a pass under which the device was lost is never saved. With the time limit lifted on the Radeon, a 7040 x 3960 pass came back black, was caught and planned again in 6 passes; the device was lost there and nothing was saved. Same Radeon after, in the automated runs: 7040 x 3960 and 8K in 4 passes of 10 Mpx at most, no ring timeout; RTX 5090: 8K still in one pass. The Legacy Viewer draws tiles of the window's size (LLViewerWindow::rawSnapshot), each a short job.
  - ⬜ To verify on Windows: an 8K photo with the photo quality on a slower or integrated GPU finishes in several parts, no TDR, no black photo.

- 🟡 A photo taken while the GPU is busy fails at once (human report, 2026-10-31; task `photo-busy-frame`; no issue; found by the human on a Radeon 610M in demo: an 8K photo with the photo quality failed 0.1 s after it started, the next try worked; validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-31 with the photo time limit's fix: eight 8K photos taken right after switching the photo quality on or off, all saved, though none happened to wait; retested after the review's fixes the same day, six large photos saved, none waited): since the stall handling (#1018), while the GPU keeps a frame past two seconds the main thread builds no frame and goes on, polling every 50 ms. The photo took a part whose frame was not built for a lost render thread and gave up on the next frame, right after the photo quality's switch to MSAA 8x had kept the GPU that long. The part stays asked, so the photo now waits for it (`photo: part <n> waits for the render thread`, then `drawn after <k> frame(s) of waiting`) and fails only when the render thread is gone, the device lost, or after 30 s of waiting (`PHOTO_WAIT`; `Renderer::drop_snapshot` keeps a late answer out of the next photo). A photo frame the GPU has not finished within the 10 s a capture is waited for is not sent again: its answer comes with a later frame (a second answer was taken for the next part). Demo with `AURORA_DEMO_GPU_STALL=690:5` and `AURORA_DEMO_SNAPSHOT=save:1920x1080`: no photo before (`the frame of part 1 was not drawn`), the photo saved after 49 frames of waiting after; the photo's frame held 15 s (`700:15`): saved after 61 frames, not sent twice; held 60 s: given up after 30 s. Not in the Legacy Viewer, which draws its snapshot synchronously (LLViewerWindow::rawSnapshot).

- 🟡 Lines across tiled photos (human request, 2026-10-29, after a resident reported lines in their snapshots; task `photo-tile-seams`; no issue; validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-29): a photo too large for one pass (4K with the photo quality, 8K, or a card short of memory) is drawn in tiles. The glow was drawn on 512 x 512 texels of each tile instead of the photo's: its halo shrank with the tile and stopped at its border. It now reads the whole photo's texels (`photo_part` in the post uniforms), as in one pass (LLPipeline::generateGlow draws it over the whole image). The bloom (346 pixels) and the depth of field (its largest blur and 66 pixels) reach past the 128-pixel guard band: the band widens to them while they are on, up to a quarter of a pass, and the drawn tiles start and end on multiples of 64, so the bloom's levels and the depth of field's tiles fall on those of one pass. The tiles are counted from their exact drawn size: fewer tiles (a 4K photo with `AURORA_DEMO_SNAPSHOT_TILE=1024`: 15 instead of 18). Measured in demo against the same photo in one pass: 247 rows or columns stepping by more than 2 levels along the seams before, 28 after (27 along lines that are not seams).
  - ⬜ To verify on the grid: a 4K photo with the photo quality (or 8K) of a scene with glowing faces, with and without the bloom and the depth of field: whole halos, no straight line along the tiles.

- 🟡 Bridge stopped after a teleport (human report, 2026-10-19; task `bridge-memory-recovery`; PR opened after a short grid check at the human's request): the grid showed a "Stack-Heap Collision" run-time error from the bridge script right after a teleport into a busy region, then every bridge request timed out and the viewer never recovered. A first grid test of the leaner 1.28 controller still showed only 5,378 bytes free at rest out of 65,536, mostly bytecode. Bridge 1.28 therefore splits the object into two scripts: the movement controller and `#Aurora Bridge Query` (`query.lsl`), which serves radar heights and script/object information with its own URL and token, announced in answer to the same probe; older bridges get only the missing script. Query bodies are read in place, avatar keys at a fixed stride, the altitude reply is built as text, and batches drop from 32 to 16 avatars. The controller's status carries `llGetFreeMemory` (Mono's lowest free memory), logged as `script memory low mark`. The viewer watches each script of a ready bridge: requests with no HTTP reply for 10 s query its running state. A stopped controller, or 90 s of controller silence, reinstalls the bridge through the Repair path (recompile, then detach/reattach save) with a chat notice, at most three times in ten minutes before leaving Repair to the user. A stopped query script is reinstalled the same way but never by silence alone, and at the limit it leaves Movelock working. Demo: `AURORA_DEMO_MOVELOCK=halted`.
  - ✅ Lock indicator off by default (human request, 2026-10-19): "Show the lock indicator" now starts unticked for new accounts; the toolbar button still shows the lock state. Accounts that already saved the option keep their choice.
  - ✅ Grid check (2026-10-19, short session): on an existing bridge the viewer added only the missing query script, both 1.28 scripts compiled, the bridge reached Ready and the controller's low mark was 10,506 bytes free (5,378 before the split).
  - ⬜ To verify on Agni (not run on the grid yet): `query service ready` in the log; radar heights of distant avatars and script/object information through the query script; several teleports into a busy region with the radar open, without a Stack-Heap Collision, and the controller's low mark after them; Movelock hold and release; automatic reinstall after unticking Running on either script of the worn bridge.

- 🟡 Bridge after a region change (human report from a grid log, 2026-10-21; task `bridge-region-change`; PR opened after a short grid check at the human's request): grid logs showed `HTTP status 404` bridge warnings after crossings and teleports, and a full bridge reinstall (recompile, detach/reattach, about 16 s without Movelock) after 13 of 30 region changes. A region change sent a worn bridge back to the install path, which recompiled it whenever the attachment reached the new region before the script's new hello; and a region change less than 3 s after the bridge became ready replayed the old region's hello, whose URL had died with the move (404s, then 6–9 s without Movelock and an HTTP error in the Movelock window). Bridge 1.29: a moved bridge waits for its new hello in Handshake (probe and running check) and is reinstalled only after 30 s without one; only a hello that renewed a live endpoint is replayed across a region change; a controller 404 (the scripts never answer 404 themselves; the query script's "unavailable" body still means a missing object) is read as a dead URL: the viewer probes for the new one instead of showing an error, and logs it at info. Both scripts answer the first probe in a new region at once, and the controller announces its renewed URL once probed, even before its first command.

- 🟡 Appearance with a large wardrobe (human report, 2026-10-24; task `outfits-window-perf`; validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-25): the frame rate fell with the Appearance window open for people with many outfits. Measured in demo with 3,000 generated outfits (`AURORA_DEMO_OUTFITS`): 31 ms a frame on the list, 36 ms on the gallery (28 to 32 fps), and 2.5 ms of interface with the window closed. Causes: every frame, the outfit folders' links were all walked and copied to find missing originals (about 25 ms), the outfits were filtered and sorted with a lower-case copy per comparison even with the window closed (2.2 ms), every header or gallery tile was laid out (4 to 6.5 ms), and each gallery tile looked for the worn outfit through the whole inventory. Now the links are walked only when the inventory changes, and then only in the outfits whose version or item count moved (`model::missing_targets`, no copy); the shown list is cached by inventory generation, filter and order, and built only when the window is drawn; the list and the gallery lay out only the rows in sight (rows out of sight keep their measured height and their automatic ids, so hover, clicks and open menus are unchanged); the worn outfit is found once a frame. Result, same scenarios, alternated passes against the previous build: 3,000 outfits, `ui` 31 → 0.65 ms on the list, 35 → 0.6 ms on the gallery, 32 → 0.8 / 36 → 0.5 ms while scrolling, 2.5 → 0.4 ms closed; 1,000 outfits, 9 to 14 ms → 0.4 to 0.5 ms. - 🟡 Inventory window frame rate (validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-16; tester report on 0.5.2, 2026-10-16: the frame rate drops for as long as the Inventory window stays open in a busy store, and recovers when it closes). Cause: the Inventory tab and the folder windows laid out every row of every open folder each frame (egui keeps the open folders between sessions, so one big folder opened once costs forever), and each inventory change rebuilt the sorted view with an ancestor walk and a set allocation per item. Fixed: the plain tree is a flat list of rows (`ui/inventory/rows.rs`), rebuilt only when the inventory, the sort or an open folder changes, and only the rows in sight are laid out, like the result tree of searches and tabs; open folders kept per window (the main window's with the UI layout, under a new key: folders opened before the update start closed once), guides and the row being renamed kept; the view rebuild dates folders and scopes trash, outfits and searches once per folder; the facts (worn, attachment points, names) are read only while a window or dialog shows them. Demo `AURORA_DEMO_INVENTORY=big[:<items>]` (30,000 items in ~3,000 folders, five levels, a 2,000 item folder open; options `recent`, `search=`, `toggle=`, `churn=`), dev build, `AURORA_FPS_LIMIT=120`, 5 alternated passes old / new: window open `u_inventory` 12.9 → 0.39 ms per frame, `ui` 13.5 → 0.84 ms, 72 → 120 fps (the cap), worst frame of the second 17.4 → 8.4 ms median and 54.8 → 8.6 ms at the 90th percentile; opening the window 50 ms → no slow frame; closed 0.11 → 0.06 ms; an inventory update with the window open 28 → 5.9 ms for its frame (3 passes). Recent (313 results) and a search (3,200 results) 0.3 ms. To verify on the grid: open the inventory in a busy place with `AURORA_PROFILE=1`, with big folders open.

## Repository and tooling

- 🔧 Loopback HTTP test servers survive Windows connection resets ([#1422](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/issues/1422), PR [#1586](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/pull/1586); task `loopback-test-servers`, 2026-10-30; tests only, no effect on the viewer): on Windows 11 26H2 the OS resets loopback connections a test server closes right after writing its reply, the client loses the reply, and `aurora-net` / `aurora-audio` tests failed in `check.ps1`. The test servers now end each connection with `aurora-net` `test_http::finish` (write side shut, socket drained until the client hangs up, 5 s at most, in its own task); the ICY stream test does the same with std sockets and reads its whole request head.
- 🔧 `Triage` Status on the project board instead of the `triage` label (human request, 2026-10-27; task `issue-triage-status`, no issue, no effect on the viewer): new `Triage` option, first of the Status field of Aurora Team Planning (added with the existing option ids, so no item lost its Status: 263 items counted before and after). New issues reach it through the board's built-in workflows ("Auto-add to project", then "Item added to project" set to `Triage`); the QA sorts them to `Todo`. `.github/workflows/issue-triage.yml` and `scripts/issue-triage.ps1` removed (the workflow was disabled on GitHub first), `triage` dropped from `scripts/setup-labels.ps1`; AGENTS.md section 15, HUMANS.md and `issue-board.ps1` updated. The 11 open issues that carried the label moved to `Triage`, then the label was deleted. The `Waiting for reporter` Status is renamed `Waiting for user response` (same option id, so its issues kept it), in AGENTS.md, HUMANS.md and `issue-board.ps1` too.
- 🟡 Privacy policy (human request, 2026-10-25; task `privacy-policy-links`; validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-25; needed for Linden Lab's Third Party Viewer Directory): the policy is written from an audit of every outbound service and every local file on main (no Aurora server; Linden Lab or the other grid chosen; GitHub for updates, news and crash reports; link previews of trusted sites; YouTube; media; GIPHY / KLIPY with the user's key) and published on the website as `/privacy/` (EN / FR). Linked from the README (Privacy section) and from Preferences › Privacy › Your data (`links::PRIVACY_POLICY`). It describes the login device identifiers (#973) and the ViewerStats report (#979) as merged. Contact: contact@aurora-viewer.org. Published on the website on 2026-10-25.
  - ⬜ QA: Preferences › Privacy › Your data › Privacy policy › Read opens the live page in the browser.
- 🟡 Fuzzing of the readers of untrusted data (human request of 2026-10-25, stability list point 1; task `fuzz-parsers`; PR authorised by the human on 2026-10-25; left: the first manual run of the Fuzz workflow after the merge): `fuzz/`, its own workspace outside the build. Thirteen targets cover what a resident or a simulator controls: JPEG2000 textures, mesh assets and sections, animations, LLSD (binary, notation, XML) and XML-RPC replies, GLTF materials and overrides, UDP packets with the object and terrain messages, compressed object updates and texture animations, texture entries, extra parameters and particle systems, prim shapes from their quantized parameters, sculpt maps of any size, terrain and wind patches, sounds, notecards, task inventories, gestures, wearables and base meshes. Seeds from our own encoders and shipped assets (a test checks every reader accepts them). `fuzz-local` (stable Rust, Windows) mutates them and reports panics, hangs over 10 s and allocations over 1 GB; the Fuzz workflow runs libFuzzer with AddressSanitizer every night on Linux, 10 minutes per target, corpus kept between runs. docs/TESTING.md "Fuzzing".
  - ⬜ Later: the readers inside the `aurora-viewer` binary crate (object cache files, scene parsers, bridge replies) cannot be called from `fuzz/`; move them into a library crate or fuzz them from tests.
  - ⬜ Upstream: symphonia-format-riff 0.6.1 multiplies two u16 WAV header fields for a log line (`wave/chunks.rs`); harmless in our builds (no overflow checks in dependencies), reported upstream.
  - ✅ The Fuzz workflow failed every night from 2026-10-26: `fuzz/Cargo.lock` fell behind whenever Dependabot updated a crate of the viewer's workspace that `fuzz/` uses by path, and `--locked` refused to update it (task `fuzz-lockfile`). `fuzz/` no longer has a lock of its own: the workflow copies the viewer's `Cargo.lock` into it, so the shipped versions are fuzzed and stay current with Dependabot; docs/TESTING.md "Fuzzing" gives the same step for local runs.
  - Found and fixed: `aurora-assets` `j2k.rs` `calc_data_size_j2c` overflowed on a SIZ header claiming 2^32 - 1 on both sides.
  - 🟡 Found by the first workflow run (2026-10-25, task `fuzz-ci-findings`; PR authorised by the human on 2026-10-25; left for QA on the grid: textures still load normally, partial / progressive downloads included) and fixed: OpenJPEG allocates a tile-part's declared length (`Psot`, up to 4 GB) before reading it; a 163-byte texture asked for 1 GB. `j2k.rs` `bound_tile_parts` sets `Psot = 0` (until the end of the codestream) on a tile-part longer than the codestream and than twice the raw pixels plus 64 KB; partial downloads keep their lengths. The second run found the same allocation behind fill bytes that OpenJPEG skips to reach the SOT (1.6 GB): every SOT marker of the codestream is now checked, not only those the header's segment lengths lead to (task `j2k-sot-scan`, follows #1027; PR authorised by the human on 2026-10-25; same QA: textures still load normally, partial downloads included). The workflow builds with `cargo fuzz run -O` so that dependencies keep their wrapping arithmetic (symphonia's harmless overflow, upstream pdeljanov/Symphonia#598).
- ✅ egui, egui-wgpu and egui-winit 0.37 (task `egui-0-37`, supersedes Dependabot #821, #822, #824; validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-22): the three move together. `Id::new` becomes `Id::unique` (same hash: saved layouts keep their keys; two real 0.36 `ui_layout.ron` files load whole), `Ui::id` / `UiBuilder::id` become `scope_id`, `WidgetType` becomes accesskit's `Role`. egui no longer has default features: `monochrome_emoji_fonts` keeps its default fonts and monochrome emoji fallbacks. The scroll offset is private: `ui/widgets/scroll_offset.rs` gives an offset decided after a show back to the area at its next show. Kinetic scrolling and rubber-banding (new) stay off. egui 0.37 regression: a click outside a focused `TextEdit` dropped its selection before the clicked button ran (field menu Cut / Copy, notecard Bold); `ui/click_away_focus.rs` takes the focus after the pass instead, as 0.36 did. egui 0.37 also sizes a text field like a button (26 points): `theme.rs` keeps 0.36's size. Text fields centre their capitals on their face (human report and choice of 2026-10-22: the place menu's SLURL field looked high, 6 points above the capitals and 9 below, on main too): `widgets::field_text_margin` lowers the text by what the font needs, for the theme's fields and the bare ones (icon fields, nav bar, chat bar, find, login, People, region restart, map search, inventory search); the amount of Pay keeps its baseline with "L$" and the script editor its gutter. Test `text_fields_centre_their_capitals_with_every_font`.
  - ⬜ later: remove `ui/click_away_focus.rs` once egui surrenders the focus only when the widget is shown (upstream fix prepared, to be reported by the human).
  - ⬜ later: epaint's `color_fonts` draws CBDT / COLR colour glyphs; it could replace the emoji pictures drawn over blank glyphs (`Emoji::text_field`).
- ⬜ wgpu 31 as soon as it is released (unblocks [#1302](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/issues/1302), on hold; human decision of 2026-10-28: wait for the release rather than patch wgpu-hal locally): crash at every launch on 6th to 9th generation Intel integrated GPUs (`igvk64`). wgpu-hal 30.0.1 creates the descriptor pool of wgpu-core's internal empty bind group layout with `poolSizeCount = 0`, which drivers older than Vulkan 1.3.215 do not accept (upstream gfx-rs/wgpu#9845). Fixed upstream by gfx-rs/wgpu#10124 (merged on trunk 2026-09-03, not backported to the 30.x branch). Move wgpu, wgpu-hal and egui-wgpu together, check `create_descriptor_pool` in `wgpu-hal/src/vulkan/descriptor.rs` carries the fix, then ask the reporter of #1302 to confirm on that release.
- ⬜ Windows CI on a Dev Drive (`samypr100/setup-dev-drive`, size to tune, order of the steps with rust-cache): to be measured against the current times
- 🔧 Shorter merge queue (task `macos-queue-speed`, 2026-10-29): since the macOS job joined the queue, an entry took 25 to 36 minutes, against 14 for the Windows tests. Measured on the runs of the day: the macOS job compiled 468 crates for its tests (8 min 19 s: main's cache held clippy's output only), ran the viewer's 5,181 tests on one runner (7 min 38 s) and built the viewer again for the demo frame (4 min); on Windows, the interface half ran 8 min, `ui::chat` (258 tests) taking half of it. Now: a push to main builds the macOS tests and the viewer for the cache (`shared-key: macos-tests`, never cancelled by the next merge); the queue runs the macOS tests on two runners (`ui::`, then the rest with the demo frame) behind the required `clippy, tests, demo (macOS)` check, without clippy (the pull request ran it); the Windows tests run in three parts (`ui::chat::`, the other `ui::`, the rest). Expected: about 10 to 12 minutes per entry, to be measured on the first queue runs.
  - ⬜ later: the `ui::chat` tests take about 1 s each on four threads; finding what each one repeats (fonts, frames) would shorten every part and `check.ps1` too.
- ✅ Build speed on a PC shared by several agents (2026-10-14, chosen by the human). Compiler cache shared by the worktrees: sccache, installed by the Aurora tools, is wired by `new-task.ps1`, `check.ps1` and the repair through `<project folder>\.cargo\config.toml` (cache in `<project folder>\.sccache`, 10 GB, `AURORA_BUILD_CACHE_SIZE`), and unwired when it is uninstalled. Measured on a clean dev build of the viewer: a new worktree takes 71 % of its crates from the cache, about a third less processor time (sum of the units 1,131–1,413 s against 1,603–2,150 s), wall time 151–207 s against 176–207 s on a loaded PC; a worktree rebuilt after its `target\` was freed, 93 %. `check.ps1` takes one of two build slots (`AURORA_BUILD_SLOTS`) for clippy and the tests. Tests always on the whole workspace (`cargo test -p` alone builds the dependencies a second time). CI: a push to main no longer lints nor tests the commit the merge queue tested, it only rebuilds the Rust cache when its key changes. rust-lld measured and not adopted: incremental rebuild of the viewer, 6 alternated passes, median 13.2 s against 14.4 s with link.exe, within the noise (±10 s).

## Network and protocol

- 🟡 Background inventory fetch (human request, 2026-10-26; task `inventory-background-fetch`; no issue; PR #1038; validated by the human on the grid on 2026-10-26): with an empty cache the inventory loaded only as folders were opened, one depth-0 AIS read per folder. Follow `LLInventoryModelBackgroundFetch::start` / `bulkFetchViaAis` / `onAISFolderCalback` / `onAISContentCalback` and `AISAPI::FetchCategorySubset`: from login on (after the cache, once the region has its capabilities), the root alone, then its folders by batches of 20 with their subtrees (`depth=50`), at most 19 reads in flight, a verify walk for what the depth limit or a failure left, and the recursive -> folder-and-content -> content fallback; the library through `LibraryAPIv3` (now requested). Marketplace listings stay with their window; folders the user opens keep their own reads and are never read twice. Deliberate difference: a root already read (the login's own read, or the cache) still loads its folders by batches instead of one recursive read each. Nested AIS replies are parsed off the main thread; folder sorting caches lowercase names. Grid, empty cache, 572 folders / 6,563 items: 6.0 s and 12 requests (one read per folder first measured 8.8 s / 65 requests). `inventory background fetch:` log line at the end; each read at debug level. Full `scripts/check.ps1` green: 5,365 passed, zero failures, 30 ignored.
  - ⬜ QA: a teleport and a region crossing while the fetch runs (the walk resumes on the new region's capabilities, `0 folders left` at the end).
  - ⬜ QA: a large inventory (tens of thousands of items): no hitch while replies are applied, no AIS throttling or 403 left unrecovered.
  - ⬜ QA: the library fully loaded through `LibraryAPIv3` (Library folders open already filled).
  - ⬜ QA: a second login with the full cache: only changed folders are read (few requests in the log line).
  - ⬜ QA: OpenSim or a grid without AIS: the `FetchInventoryDescendents2` fallback still walks the whole tree.
- 🟡 Linden Lab's viewer statistics (no issue; task `viewer-stats`; the Third Party Viewer Policy's clause on the viewer statistics packet; validated by the human on the grid on 2026-10-25: arrival and 5-minute reports accepted): Aurora asked for the `ViewerStats` capability and never posted to it. The session now posts send_viewer_stats' LLSD (indra/newview/llviewerstats.cpp) once the agent has arrived, every 5 minutes (SEND_STATS_PERIOD) and before the LogoutRequest (LLAppViewer::requestQuit), with the Legacy Viewer's fields and types: agent (start / run / foreground time, foreground fps, the frame time jitter of updateFrameStats, version "Aurora Viewer <x.y.z.n>", language, sim_fps, avatars in view, average ping, distance travelled, regions visited, resident memory, translation off), system (RAM, OS, CPU and its SSE levels, threads, the network adapter's address as `xx-xx-xx-xx-xx-xx` like send_viewer_stats (`machine_id::adapter_mac`, the adapter LLUUID::getNodeID picks, zeros without one) and the login's hashed `id0` as `serial_number`, both never logged, the GPU's name, vendor, driver, VRAM and largest texture, the API "Vulkan" where the Legacy Viewer gives OpenGL's version, GPU class -1 unknown, shader level 3 to 5 from shadows / AO), downloads (texture and mesh bytes; world and object 0, as the Legacy Viewer never adds to them), the message system's counters (zero-coded packets and savings in, out, send failures, lost, resent, failed resends, off-circuit, invalid), inventory usable, display name settings. The Legacy Viewer's own choices are kept: no preferences in the last report, no `ui` block, no setting to turn it off. A failed post is logged at debug level only, without the capability's URL; any 2xx answer counts as posted. The logged copies of the report show the adapter address and the serial as `(not logged)`, and the session id is added after logging. Quitting waits for the last report, 2 s at most and no longer than it takes (`NetClient::wait_viewer_stats`); Log out to the login screen keeps the network runtime, so it finishes on its own. Demo `AURORA_DEMO_VIEWER_STATS=1` logs the report once, nothing sent.
  - ⬜ QA: the logout report accepted (`viewer statistics posted to the simulator` at logout, with `RUST_LOG=info,aurora_net=debug`), after Log out and after quitting.
  - ⬜ QA: Linux (the adapter address, the reports accepted).
  - ⬜ QA: a long session (one report every 5 minutes, crossings and teleports counted in regions visited and distance).
  - ⬜ QA: no identifier in the logs (no MAC, serial or session id).
- 🟡 Login device ids like the official viewer (Third Party Viewer Policy, human's decision 2026-10-25; task `login-machine-id`; no issue; validated by the human on 2026-10-25): `mac` and `id0` were the md5 of a random UUID drawn at installation, so a reinstall gave a new device and machine bans could not hold. They are now computed as llHashedUniqueID and generateSerialNumber do (`machine_id.rs`): `mac` is the md5 of LLMachineID's six bytes (the Win32_ComputerSystemProduct UUID folded, else the Win32_OperatingSystem serial, else the NetBIOS adapter address, else 32 zeros; the first adapter address on Linux), `id0` the md5 of the C: volume serial (empty when unreadable) or of the longest /dev/disk/by-uuid name; `host_id` is sent empty, as the HostID setting. Computed once at startup off the UI thread; only the source kind is logged, never an identifier. Unlike the Legacy Viewer, the process-wide CoInitializeSecurity is not called (the proxy blanket is enough for these reads). On this PC, `mac` equals the System ID the Legacy Viewer logged, and `id0` the hash of the volume serial read independently. The random `machine_id` setting is gone.
  - ⬜ QA: a normal login on Windows and on Linux.
  - ⬜ QA: a VM or a machine with no network adapter falls back cleanly (login still works).
  - ⬜ QA: no identifier in the logs (only "login device ids computed: mac from …, id0 from …").
- 🟡 Quick login after a sudden close or a logout (#956; task `quick-relogin`; validated by the human on the grid on 2026-10-25: log out → immediate login shows the 10 s countdown): a login right after a crash, a killed viewer or a Log out to the same account landed in a region still logging the previous session out, and the avatar stayed frozen until the 90 s time-out. The login now tells the login server of a session that did not end cleanly (`last_exec_event` LAST_EXEC_UNKNOWN, `last_exec_duration`, `last_exec_session_id`, as the Legacy Viewer reads them from its exec marker; Aurora always sent 0 and no session id). A "presence" refusal (LoginFailedPendingLogout…) shows the grid's words and is tried again after 60 s, three times in a row at most. The AgentMovementComplete time-out sends a LogoutRequest before going back to the login screen, as STATE_AGENT_WAIT does. Per account (`login_wait.rs`, `last_sessions.json`), the last session's id, its sign of life every 15 s and its end: a login waits 10 s after a session the viewer saw end, 60 s after the last sign of life of one it never saw end, with a countdown in the connection progress (Escape cancels). Demo `AURORA_DEMO_LOGIN_WAIT=logout|sudden|refused`.
  - ⬜ QA: Escape during the countdown, then repeated immediate logins.
  - ⬜ QA: a killed viewer, then an immediate login (the 60 s wait from the last sign of life).
  - ⬜ QA: Escape, then an immediate login after a kill: does the grid now answer "presence" (the 60 s retry countdown) since it knows the previous session id?
  - ⬜ QA: two accounts: logging one out never holds the other back.
  - ⬜ QA: note the observed durations, to tune the 10 s / 60 s constants (`login_wait.rs`).

- 🟡 Stability: never lose a session to a blip (2026-10-17). The main simulator's circuit is dead after 100 s of silence as in the Legacy Viewer (llstartup.cpp `circuit_timeout`, was 60 s here: a laggy region or a short outage cut the session). From 5 s of silence a discreet pill under the top bar says the viewer waits for the region and counts the seconds (`ui/link_health.rs`; the Legacy Viewer gives no sign before "connection lost"). A lost link (silence, the main event queue given up after its 15 retries, the region closing the circuit, the arrival never completed) now says so and the next login goes back to the region and the spot the user was in (`uri:` start, same grid and account; a kick does not offer it): the Legacy Viewer goes back to the usual start location. A session that ends while the frame holds the window (the cursor locked by an orbit or mouselook) now gives the cursor back at the end of that frame instead of leaving it hidden and locked. `AURORA_DEMO_LINK=stall:<frame>[:<seconds>],lost:<frame>`. The objects the isolation left out noted no texture use at all, so under memory pressure their textures were lowered to their coarsest level (demo: 500 MB of textures down to 6 MB) and the return to the entire scene had to reload them all at once, with the video memory already full. - 🟡 GPU device lost in busy places with the video memory over the driver's budget ([#1561](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/issues/1561), duplicate #1559; task `vram-over-budget`, 2026-10-30; validated by the human on the grid on 2026-10-30, a region with 35 avatars, with the card's own budget and with `AURORA_VRAM_BUDGET_MB=7000`; to verify: no new device-lost report from the testers): five crash reports (#1374, #1490, #1553, #1559, #1561) showed the video memory at or over the budget with the texture memory pressure stuck at 1 or 2 of 7. The pressure rose past a step only once every reduction it listed was done, which a busy, streaming scene never reaches: each pass lists new ones (demo, `AURORA_DEMO_STREAM=6000,100` with `AURORA_VRAM_BUDGET_MB=2048`: 14 s at step 1, up to 2,384 MB for a 2,048 MB budget). It now also rises 3 s after the last step while still above the target, done or not, as the Legacy Viewer raises its bias all the while it is above the target (LLViewerTexture::updateClass). Grid, 7,000 MB budget: step 1 to 4 in 6 s, the video memory at 5.9 GB at most, no visible change. Where step 1 is enough (the card's own budget, demo budgets of 3 and 4 GB), nothing changes.
  - ⬜ later: in a busy region the pressure goes 0 → 1 → 0 about once a minute (about 1,500 textures lowered, then loaded again), the loop the step-down rule is meant to avoid: at step 1 the step below is estimated as what the pages hold now. And after a large arrival under a tight budget the pressure stays a step or two higher than needed: the step-down estimate scales the textures by the pages' free room, 1.7 times after a mass lowering in demo (2,048 MB budget: step 4 and 64 MB of textures where step 2 held 199 MB before this change).

- 🟡 Stack overflow on a background job thread while logging in among many objects ([#1689](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/issues/1689); task `texture-read-stack-overflow`, 2026-11-01; validated by the human in demo on 2026-11-01, `AURORA_DEMO_STREAM=6000,6000`: responsive, textures filled in; to verify: no new report with this signature from a busy region): a tester's 0.8.3 crashed 145 s after login (116,395 objects, 4 regions) with `0xC00000FD` in `texture_cache::read`. `Jobs::spawn_many` ran each batch as a parallel loop inside a pool job; a pool thread waiting in that loop runs other queued jobs, the next batches' loops among them, which nested on its 2 MB stack without bound. Each batch now queues its items as separate jobs (`rayon::spawn_fifo`, in order) from its one pool job: nothing waits on a pool thread, so nothing nests. Unit test `batches_of_jobs_do_not_nest_on_a_thread_stack`: 238 KB of nesting in 0.4 s before, none after. Demo, 2,000 objects at once: settled in 7.9 s before / 6.7 s after, worst frame 24.4 / 24.0 ms.
- 🟡 A graphics card that stops answering no longer freezes the viewer (task `gpu-hang-recovery`, 2026-10-25; PR authorised by the human on 2026-10-25; grid checks by QA: on a PC where the viewer used to stay white or frozen after login, the window keeps answering and the "graphics card is not responding" box shows; No closes and logs out within a few seconds; the next start offers the safe graphics, "Use" switches to Potato, "Restore my graphics" puts the earlier settings back; a normal session shows no box and no card; a tester's window stayed white and frozen after login with no crash report: the main thread waited for the render thread without a bound). The renderer now waits at most 2 s for the render thread before building a frame (`Renderer::stalled_for`); while the GPU holds a frame no frame is built (the stores keep their writes, the interface's texture changes are carried over), the window keeps answering, sound and chat go on. After 6 s a native message box says the graphics card does not answer, with what to try, and asks to keep waiting (again a minute later) or to close (logged out, ended within a few seconds even if the render thread never comes back; the close button does the same, the exit prompt cannot be drawn); it goes away by itself when frames come again. The render thread's stack goes to the crash session (`gpu-stall.txt`), reported as `GPU not responding` (triage signature `gpu stall`). A session ended with the GPU in trouble (stall, device loss, frozen window) leaves a mark the next start consumes: the login screen offers the safe graphics (the Potato level, applied only on the user's click, the level's values kept aside in `graphics-before-safe.json` and offered back on the same card). The Legacy Viewer has a safe start chosen by hand (`--safe`, `LLFeatureManager::setSafe`) and no stall notice. `AURORA_DEMO_GPU_STALL`, `AURORA_DEMO_SAFE_GRAPHICS`.
  - ⬜ Later: after a device loss, rebuild the renderer from the CPU-side caches (stores' mirrors, decoded textures in the cache) instead of ending the session; then a stall that turns into a device loss could recover without a restart
- 🟡 Crash reports that can be acted on (task `crash-report-detail`, human request of 2026-10-25 after #978, #989 and #1001; demo `freeze` scenario run here, PR authorised by the human on 2026-10-25; left: a real report from a tester's freeze or crash on a release build: three "unexpected shutdown" reports with no stack and 17 identical "additional diagnostic" lines). A watchdog thread (`crash/watchdog.rs`) writes the session's sign of life every 5 s (`alive.txt`: time, last time the window answered, memory, and the state `app/crash_state.rs` notes every 2 s: screen, frame rate, window size, graphics preset, video memory, texture pressure, objects, avatars, regions). When Windows considers the window hung (`IsHungAppWindow`, the "Not responding" test; the Legacy Viewer's LLWatchdog ends the viewer itself, this one only observes), it suspends the main and render threads in turn and unwinds their stacks into `freeze.txt` (`native::write_thread_stack`: registers, `RtlLookupFunctionEntry` / `RtlVirtualUnwind` inside the suspended thread's stack, no allocation or lock while suspended). A session ended frozen is reported as `Freeze` with both stacks (the triage signs and names it `Crash: freeze in …`); a session whose watcher died with it gets its duration from the last sign of life and says whether Windows started again right after (system crash, power loss). The watcher hears Windows end the session (hidden window, `WM_ENDSESSION`): a shutdown is no longer reported. Reports also give the exit code's usual meaning, "GPU device lost" (new device-lost callback in aurora-render), a "Last state" table, and warnings as `-<s> s | level | Rust module | kind` with repeats folded. The crash window asks what the tester was doing (a few words needed before publishing, whatever the Preferences say: Always now opens straight on the report to publish instead of sending it by itself) and whether their graphics drivers are up to date (driver found shown beside it). `AURORA_DEMO_CRASH=freeze`.
  - ✅ Crash reports name the overlay hooks of the session (task `crash-overlay-name`, #1342, validated in demo by the human on 2026-10-28: a freeze at login after an overlay hook arrived and the GPU was lost, the report only said "overlay hook loaded"). Each known hook that arrives (`overlay_hooks.rs`) is added to `overlay-hooks.txt` in the crash session; the report gets an "Overlay hooks" row (program and file), checked again against the fixed list, however long ago the hook came (the log's tail may no longer hold its line). `AURORA_DEMO_OVERLAY_HOOK=<file>`. The freeze of #1342 itself (0.8.1, before the device loss handling of #1275) waits for the tester's answer.
  - 🟡 Blind crashes and silent thread deaths (task `crash-blind-spots`, human request of 2026-10-25; PR authorised by the human on 2026-10-25; grid checks by QA). Out of memory: the allocator (`allocator.rs`) hands a failed allocation to `native::out_of_memory`, which writes its size and stack to the pre-opened `oom.txt` without allocating, before the standard library aborts; a fast fail after it is reported as `Out of memory (N bytes)` with that stack (a handled failure, `try_reserve`, is not). Stack overflow: a vectored handler writes the stack as soon as the exception is raised (`Native exception 0xC00000FD`). Silent thread death: `crash/threads.rs` names the long-lived threads the session cannot do without (`aurora-net` runtime, `aurora-pages`, `aurora-trash`, `aurora-cache`, `aurora-texcache`, `aurora-chatlog`, `aurora-transcript`); their panic, which left the viewer running without them, now ends the session at the next frame, the window says "A part of the viewer stopped working" and the report adds `| Thread | … |`. Triage reads `Out of memory`. `AURORA_DEMO_CRASH=oom|overflow|thread`.
  - ⬜ Later: other fast fails (`abort`, a double panic, a security check) still have no stack: Windows Error Reporting local dumps; restart a dead non-critical thread instead of ending the session where that is safe
  - ⬜ sleep / resume: check that `Instant` keeps counting during sleep on Windows (QueryPerformanceCounter); if not, a long sleep would not end a dead circuit until 100 s after waking

- 🟡 Region without terrain or objects (Agni, 2026-10-09, login at Yikes: no RegionHandshake processed, only the ocean all the way; relaunching was enough). The simulator sends terrain and objects only after our RegionHandshakeReply, and Firestorm has neither retry nor timeout for this message (process_region_handshake): its only protection is the circuit. Aligned with LLMessageSystem::checkMessages: a reliable packet is acknowledged (and remembered against duplicates) only once decoded and processed, so the simulator resends an unreadable message instead of it being lost (before: acknowledged on receipt). Login like llstartup.cpp: UseCircuitCode resent every 5 s, 3 times (UseCircuitCodeTimeout / MaxRetries), CompleteAgentMovement only after its acknowledgement (before: sent anyway after 2 s), back to the login screen with the LoginPacketNeverReceived message if it never arrives. Log: decoding failures as warnings (message, region, sequence, limited per message), "region handshake from …" at each handshake, warning if the arrival region has not sent its own 10 s after AgentMovementComplete (counters of packets, failures, duplicates, dropped packets). No demo scenario (the demo does not go through the UDP circuit): unit tests of the circuit and of RegionHandshake decoding. Validated by the human on Agni on 2026-10-09 ("Test handshake-region": login at Yikes, TP to Tordangle and back, handshake of each region logged, no failure); as the original bug is random, to be watched in the logs (`no RegionHandshake`, `failed to decode`)
- ⬜ Later, to be decided: alert to the user when the arrival region has not sent its RegionHandshake (today, warning in the log only, 10 s after AgentMovementComplete): explain that the terrain and the objects will not arrive and offer to reconnect. Visible difference: Firestorm has neither alert nor retry for this message

An outfit change refused while the new region had no capabilities set the current outfit and the outfit folders back to unloaded without asking for them again (`AppearanceUi::refresh`), and only the open Appearance window asked for them: every later change was refused for the rest of the session. Now, like the Legacy Viewer: a new seed drops the region's old capabilities until the new ones arrive (LLViewerRegion::setSeedCapability); a failed folder fetch is asked again once per change of region, then every failed folder when the agent's region gets its capabilities (LLInventoryModelBackgroundFetch waits for capabilitiesReceived, BGFolderHttpHandler::processFailure requeues); a refused outfit change asks again for the current outfit, the outfits and their missing link targets, so "still loading" lasts until they arrive. Unit tests of the crossing (fetch lost then asked again on the new capabilities) and of the refused change. To verify on Agni: walk and fly into a neighbour, then right after and a minute later wear an item, attach an object, take one off, open a folder of the inventory; the same after a teleport. Tried by the human on Agni on 2026-10-16: the inventory and wearing keep working after a region crossing
- 🟡 Outfits with a broken link (#1441, task `outfit-broken-links`; reported with a 192,000-item inventory and 78 outfits: "This outfit's inventory is still loading" forever, no outfit change possible). A link whose original was deleted held its outfit, and the current outfit, on "still loading" for good, and one deleted original made the whole AIS read of the 15 items asked with it fail. Now, like the Legacy Viewer (LLAppearanceMgr::updateAppearanceFromCOF waits only while the inventory is fetched, then wears without the broken link): each item read has its own outcome (`ais::read_items`; for FetchInventory2, an item absent from a valid answer), an item the server answers 404 / 410 is a broken link's original (`Inventory::missing_items`), a failed read is asked again up to 3 times then counts as broken; outfits and the current outfit are complete once every link is read or broken, Wear / Add / Take off / Save skip broken links (logged) and the rewritten folders drop them. Demo `AURORA_DEMO_APPEARANCE=broken`. Unit tests of both cases, of the retries and of the two read paths. Validated in demo and by the automated tests on 2026-10-30. To verify on Agni (QA team): an outfit holding a link to a deleted original (copy a clothing item, save an outfit with it, delete the copy and empty the Trash) is worn with Replace and with Add, without the deleted item and without "still loading"; another outfit can be worn afterwards; the outfit folder's right click in Inventory offers Replace outfit, not greyed.
  - ✅ "The inventory server is not available yet" after a region change (#750, task `wear-after-region-change`): nothing could be worn or attached after a crossing or a teleport into a region already open as a neighbour. The first answer to a neighbour's seed lacks the inventory capabilities (74 against 77 for the agent's region in a grid log), and the crossing or EstablishAgentCommunication that makes it the agent's region repeats the same seed, which Aurora ignored: the region kept the neighbour's capabilities without `InventoryAPIv3`. Now, like LLViewerRegion::setSeedCapability, the same seed again is asked a second time beside the first request and the answer that grants more capabilities replaces the first (requestBaseCapabilitiesCompleteCoro); the event queue and the region features keep going. A new seed from EstablishAgentCommunication now drops the old capabilities too (it was only stored, and the region could stay without capabilities if the answer to the old seed was still on its way). Unit test `a_repeated_seed_is_asked_again_and_the_larger_answer_kept`; full `scripts/check.ps1` green (3,231 viewer tests). Validated by the human on Agni on 2026-10-21: after walking into a neighbour, a teleport to a neighbour and a teleport to a distant region, items are worn and attached; the log shows the second answer granting 77 capabilities where the neighbour's first had 74 (crossing and teleport to a neighbour), and 77 at once for the distant region

- 🟡 Running (SetAlwaysRun on a double tap), flying, crouching
  - 🟡 Stopping a flight keeps its momentum, as in Firestorm: Aurora sent a STOP (`AGENT_CONTROL_STOP`, the simulator's brake) with the end of the flight, so the avatar dropped straight down in both movement modes; Firestorm only clears the FLY flag (LLAgent::toggleFlying → setFlying, llagent.cpp) and the avatar falls on with the flight's speed. `App::toggle_fly` now does the same. With Aurora's movement the avatar then *coasts* (`own_motion.rs`, `Prediction::coasting`): while the simulator carries it faster than the keys ask, the lead goes from the flight's (3 m at 16 m/s) to the keys' at 3 m/s at most, instead of a walk's lead at once (on Agni the drawn speed fell from 15.8 to 4.9 m/s, then rushed at 27); what is left at the landing stays where it is drawn and fades. No speed is learned from reports in the air (vertical speed over 1 m/s, or a coast), nor a speed of the land over twice its usual one: the fall with momentum, forward held, had taught a walk of 11.9 m/s, and the walks after it ran 3 m ahead then dropped their lead. Unit test of the Agni case: no frame below 13 m/s before the landing (7.6 m/s without the coast). The flight's ramp starts at 0.5 s instead of none (Agni: from a hover, 90 % of the speed 0.55 s after the first report that moved): a flight of a moment while walking (fly pressed twice quickly) led by 2.9 m, the drawn avatar rushing at 14 m/s then standing still while the simulator caught up. Checked on Agni on 2026-10-16 (four sessions with `AURORA_OWN_MOTION_TRACE=1`): the end of a flight keeps its momentum, the drawn speed stays within 3 to 5 m/s of the simulator's (before: −11.7 to +12.1, up to 27.6 m/s), falls at rest and from a car roof are followed (0.8 m of glide at most), the learned walk stays 3.2 m/s. ⬜ To verify on Agni: the flight's ramp at a take-off and at a quick fly, fly.
  - 🟡 A session that ends flying logs in flying again (human request, 2026-10-16), the Legacy Viewer's `FlyingAtExit`: saved at logout, quit or disconnection (`LLAppViewer::disconnectViewer`, llappviewer.cpp), the FLY control set at login before the first AgentUpdate (`LLAgent::init`, llagent.cpp). Kept per account here (`world/flying_at_exit.rs`, the account's `flying_at_exit.json`; the Legacy Viewer keeps one value for the whole PC). A region that blocks flying now lands the avatar at its arrival and when its flags change (`process_agent_movement_complete`, `process_region_info`, llviewermessage.cpp; before, Aurora kept a flight there), and a login seated on an object stops the flight as before. The demo keeps no state. Unit tests: the saved state per account, the no-fly landing. ⬜ To verify on Agni: log out flying, log in again (flying), log out walking (walking), log in flying into a no-fly region (lands).
