- 🟡 Classic avatars: alpha / transparency issues, especially their hair, and incorrect shape rendering (reported by the human on 2026-10-13 with a screenshot, which this fix did not have at hand: both causes were found in the code and reproduced in demo). **Alpha**: a system body part took its pass from the alpha class of its bake alone, so a body whose bake holds soft alpha was drawn with the blended faces (see-through, without depth), and its masks were cut at 0.5. Now as `LLVOAvatar::renderSkinned` / `renderTransparent`, drawn by `LLDrawPoolAvatar`: head, upper and lower body and eyes in the opaque passes, alpha-tested at 0.2 (`sMinimumAlpha`) and never blended; hair, eyelashes and skirt blended where their bake is, and alpha-tested as well (0.2, skirt 0.25: `fs_blend` tests a blended record that also carries the mask flag; its shadow stays that of a blended face). **Shape**: the vertex morphs of the system body were not applied, so everyone had the female mesh of the files, with its face and its hair. `scene/morph.rs` ports `LLPolyMorphTarget::apply` (positions, softened normals, texture coordinates; 240 morphs over head, upper and lower body, hair, eyelashes and skirt; a parameter made for the other sex keeps its default weight). A part is built by a job for a set of weights and shared by the avatars that have them (`GeomKey::AvatarMorph`); it is drawn unmorphed until it is ready, and a hidden part (mesh bodies, alpha layers) is not built. Deliberate difference from Firestorm, which writes the depth of the blended hair: Aurora's blended faces do not, the hair is sorted with them. Demo `AURORA_DEMO_CLASSIC=1` (docs/TESTING.md): the band of soft alpha at the waist showed the sky through the body before, solid now; male build and long hair for ours, heavy build for the wolf. Tests: pass and record flags of each part, morph parameters read per mesh and masked ones left out, a morph applied at its weight with its normals, male torso against the female one, the demo shapes read back from their appearance values. Validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-13. To verify on Agni, next to Firestorm: classic avatars of both sexes (build, face, system hair and its tips, eyelashes, skirt), one with an alpha layer and one with a tattoo or clothes of soft alpha, and mesh avatars unchanged.
  - ⬜ Later: the seven morphs that wait for a mask taken from a bake (`<morph_masks>` of avatar_lad.xml: loose shirt and trousers, flared sleeves and legs, long cuffs, low crotch, facial hair), which Firestorm applies once the bake is loaded (`LLVOAvatar::onBakedTextureMasksLoaded`); the levels of detail of the system meshes (`avatar_*_1.llm`…).

- 🟡 Eyelashes seen through mesh hair (human report on Agni, 2026-10-16, side by side with the Legacy Viewer). Cause: the blended faces were sorted back to front by the distance of their object only and none wrote depth; eyelashes, a small object in front of the face, came after hair centred on the head and were drawn over it. The Legacy Viewer draws the blended faces of rigged meshes in a pass of their own before the others, writing depth (`LLDrawPoolAlpha::render`: `forwardRender(true)` then `forwardRender()`, `write_depth = rigged`, fragments under 1/255 of alpha dropped), so a layer in front hides what is behind it whichever is drawn first. Now the same: `scene/blend_order.rs` puts the rigged blended faces (worn rigged meshes, animesh) first, back to front among themselves (the Legacy Viewer keeps an attachment order there), then the others back to front, with a fixed order for faces at the same distance (`DrawLists::blend_depth`); scene pass B is cut around them, a part of its own writing depth (pipeline `blend rigged`). Classic avatars' system hair is unchanged (line above). `AURORA_RIGGED_BLEND=sorted` keeps the former drawing, `alt` alternates it one second in three (`xmode=`). Demo `AURORA_DEMO_HAIR=1,48,20 AURORA_DEMO_LASHES=1`: a red ball worn inside the hair, on the camera's side, showed through the strands (148 red pixels in SMAA, 156 in MSAA 4x) and no longer does (0); the rest of the image unchanged (SMAA: no other pixel; MSAA 4x: a few avatar edge samples, as between two runs of the same build). Cost, demo crowd of 40 each wearing 8 layers, alternated in one session (shared PC): `g_transparent` +0.04 ms in SMAA (0.07 → 0.11) and in MSAA 4x (1.47 → 1.51), `gpu` +0.07 to +0.13 ms. Tests: order of the rigged and other faces, the former order, a fixed order at equal distance. Validated by the human on Agni on 2026-10-16, side by side with the Legacy Viewer: the eyelashes no longer show through mesh hair; face, glasses, chains and collar layers fine. Still to check on Agni: hair in front of glass, glass and particles in front of and behind hair, layered mesh clothes, animesh with fur, MSAA.
  - 🟡 Halo around an avatar in front of glass ([#556](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/issues/556), 2026-10-17): the rigged blended faces wrote their depth from 1/255 of alpha, as the Legacy Viewer does (`LLDrawPoolAlpha::forwardRender(true)`, `MINIMUM_ALPHA`), so the nearly transparent fringe of fur, feathers or hair hid the glass, water and particles drawn after it: a ring around the avatar where the glass was missing. Their depth is now written only where they are at least half covered: a depth pass with that alpha test (`fs_depth_contact`), then their colour, back to front, depth tested and not written (`DrawLists::blend_depth_alpha_test`). Deliberate improvement on the Legacy Viewer: an opaque strand still hides the eyelashes under it, but they now show through the see-through gaps between strands, as the scene behind does. Also: blended faces no longer take the screen-space occlusion and indirect light, which are those of what lies behind them (`screen_terms`; the Legacy Viewer's alpha pass applies neither). `AURORA_RIGGED_BLEND=depth05|write|sorted|alt`, `AURORA_BLEND_AO=old|new|alt`, demo `AURORA_DEMO_HALO=1`. Demo (SMAA and MSAA): no ring with `AURORA_DEMO_HAIR=8,24,60,16`; the lashes ball of `AURORA_DEMO_HAIR=1,48,20` hidden by the strands, seen in their gaps (80 red pixels against 0 with `write`, 155 with `sorted`); cost of the depth pass within noise (crowd of 40, 8 layers: `gpu` 1.440 → 1.445 ms, `g_transparent` 0.242 → 0.243 ms). Stacked fine-strand layers show some alpha-test aliasing between layers.
  - ⬜ to check on Agni (the human asked for the PR on 2026-10-17 before testing it there): the ring gone in front of glass and translucent objects, with fur, feathers and soft hair (the reported avatar); eyelashes under mesh hair, close up (seen through the gaps between strands, hidden by the strands); thin layered hair (the inner layer showing more, stair-step aliasing near the neck); particles and water behind hair; MSAA and SMAA; `AURORA_RIGGED_BLEND=alt` to compare with `write`

- 🟡 Ambient occlusion line down the middle of asymmetric mesh heads ([#882](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/issues/882), 2026-10-23; task `blend-face-ao`; validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-23, the grid checks left to QA). Cause: since #556 a blended face takes no screen-space occlusion (the occlusion came from the opaque depth, so it was that of what lies behind the face); a head whose halves differ in alpha mode (one blended though opaque to the eye) had one half occluded, the other not. Both occlusion methods now read a copy of the depth prepass with the blended faces at least half covered drawn over it (`fs_depth_contact`, the contact shadows' rule), and those faces take the occlusion and GTAO's indirect light like the opaque ones (`BLEND_SCREEN_DEPTH`, common.wgsl); more transparent ones still take none. Deliberate improvement on the Legacy Viewer, whose alpha pass applies no occlusion: such faces also occlude what is around them (the floor under a blended mesh body). With the contact shadows on, their pass copies that depth instead of drawing the blended faces again. `AURORA_BLEND_AO=new|none|old|alt`, demo `AURORA_DEMO_BLEND_AO=1`. Demo (GTAO and Legacy, occlusion view): with `none` the occlusion around the nose stops at the middle line and the blended half stays white, now it runs across both halves; no halo back with `AURORA_DEMO_HALO=1` and `AURORA_DEMO_HAIR=8,24,60,16`. Cost (crowd of 40 with 8 hair layers, GTAO High, SMAA, 120 fps cap, three alternated runs, medians): `g_ssao` 0.343–0.361 → 0.368–0.387 ms, `g_contact` 0.121 → 0.106 ms, `gpu` unchanged (about 1.68 ms).
  - ⬜ to check on Agni (QA testers): an asymmetric mesh head under a hat or hair, occlusion on, GTAO then Legacy: no line down the middle of the face; a blended mesh body or hair still occluded naturally (no dark patch, no halo) and the floor under it; glass and translucent objects in front of an avatar: no halo (#556); MSAA and SMAA; `AURORA_BLEND_AO=alt` to compare with the behaviour of before
- 🟡 Layered mesh hair: see-through strands and stair steps where layers overlap ([#935](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/issues/935), 2026-10-24; task `hair-alpha-sorting`; validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-25, the grid checks left to QA). Cause: since #556 the rigged blended faces wrote their depth where at least half covered in a pass before any of their colour, so a layer drawn first was hidden behind every strand of the layers over it from 50 % on; such a strand, 50 to 99 % opaque, then showed the skull or the sky behind the hair instead of the layer under it, with stair steps along its 50 % contour. The faces of one object were also ordered by their draw record, which the allocator hands out in any order. The Legacy Viewer draws the rigged blended faces writing depth from 1/255 as they go, without sorting them by distance: per avatar, the last attachment point first and, on one point, the last attached first (LLVOAvatar::idleUpdateMisc `draw_order`, LLSpatialGroup::CompareRenderOrder), the faces of a linkset in their order (LLVolumeGeometryManager::genDrawInfo); hair is made for that order. Now the same (`RiggedBlendDepth::Layered`, `scene/blend_order.rs` `RigOrder`: skeletons back to front, then attachment point, the root's local id for the attachment order, the prims by local id, the faces by face then first index), drawn into a copy of the scene depth (`Targets::blend_layers`); the scene depth takes them only where at least half covered, as before, so no halo comes back in front of glass (#556). `AURORA_RIGGED_BLEND=depth05` draws as before, `alt` alternates it; the hair demo now attaches its inner layer last, as a hair made for the Legacy Viewer. Demo (`AURORA_DEMO_HAIR=8,24,60,16`, SMAA and MSAA 4x): the see-through outer layers and the moiré of `depth05` are gone, the hair matches `write` (the Legacy Viewer's drawing: mean difference 1.1 / 255 between two consecutive runs, 17 between two runs of one mode); `AURORA_DEMO_HALO=1`: no ring, which `write` shows; `AURORA_DEMO_LASHES=1`: the lashes ball, attached after the hair, is drawn first and seen through the strands as with `write`. Cost (crowd of 40 with 8 layers, 120 fps cap, alternated in one session, medians): `g_transparent` 0.144 → 0.191 ms in SMAA and 0.223 → 0.298 ms in MSAA 4x, `gpu` +0.02 / +0.07 ms; one more depth target of the window's size and samples.
  - ⬜ to check on Agni (QA testers): real layered mesh hairs on the human's and the reporter's avatars (no see-through strands, no stair steps); tails; hair made of several prims; eyelashes under a fringe; hair in front of glass and translucent objects (no #556 halo); a side-by-side with the Legacy Viewer; GPU time (`g_transparent`) and memory in a busy region, SMAA and MSAA; `AURORA_RIGGED_BLEND=alt` to compare with the drawing of before
  - 🟡 Regression of #948 (reported by the tester on 2026-10-25: "very strange patterns on their hair textures"; task `hair-alpha-regression`; validated by the human on the grid on 2026-10-25, the full grid checks left to QA): triangular shards where the scene shows through some hairs. The Legacy Viewer's rule, reread: rigged blended faces write depth (lldrawpoolalpha.cpp:241, 249) from alpha 0.004 (lldrawpoolalpha.cpp:64, 130; alphaF.glsl discard), in the attachment order; but it reorders the triangles of every mesh face for the vertex cache (llvolume.cpp:2720, 5881, `meshopt_optimizeVertexCache`), so the cards of one face overlap in no particular order and a soft strand edge drawn first hides the strands drawn after it behind it. #948 drew exactly that and showed the shards. Now (`RiggedBlendDepth::Runs`, the default): the rigged faces' depth where nearly opaque (95 %, `fs_depth_opaque`) before any of their colour, then attachment point by attachment point of each skeleton (`blend_order::rig_runs`) their colour, depth tested, and their depth where half covered; the copy of the depth of #948 is made only for `AURORA_RIGGED_BLEND=copy`. Demo `AURORA_DEMO_HAIR_CARDS=120` (one face of 120 shuffled soft cards), SMAA and MSAA 4x: the shards of `copy` are gone; `AURORA_DEMO_HAIR=8,24,60,16`: as dense as #948 (no see-through layers of `depth05`); `AURORA_DEMO_HALO=1`: no ring; `AURORA_DEMO_LASHES=1`: as `write`. Cost (crowd of 40 with 8 layers, alternated with `depth05` in one session, medians): `g_transparent` 0.148 → 0.211 ms in SMAA, 0.206 → 0.256 ms in MSAA 4x, `gpu` +0.05 ms; one run per worn mesh instead of per point measured at about +0.3 ms.
    - ⬜ to check on Agni (QA testers): the reporter's and other layered hairs, close up and from a few metres (no shards, no see-through layers); tails; hair made of several prims; eyelashes under a fringe; hair in front of glass (no #556 halo); a side-by-side with the Legacy Viewer (does it show the shards on the same hair?); GPU time (`g_transparent`) in a busy region with SMAA and MSAA
  - 🟡 Still present on 0.7.5 / 0.7.6 (the tester, 2026-10-25: darker patches the shape of triangles inside the strands; task `hair-shards-935`; PR authorised by the human on 2026-10-25, the tester's checks on the next release left). Cause found in demo, the reporter's hair not reproduced: with #966's drawing (`runs`), a strand between 50 and 95 % hides nothing drawn after it, so an inner layer drawn after the outer one, darker, shows over it in patches bounded by its triangles (`AURORA_DEMO_HAIR_CARDS=160,layered,outer`). New default (`RiggedBlendDepth::Split`): run by run (a new one for each mesh worn on a point that already has one), what is at least half covered is drawn first writing its depth as it is drawn, as the Legacy Viewer's 1/255, then the fainter texels, depth tested only: no inner layer over an outer one, no shards from a soft edge (#966), the layers of #948 as dense as `copy`, no #556 halo. The triangles of every mesh face are now drawn in the Legacy Viewer's order (`aurora_assets::legacy_triangle_order`, end of `LLVolumeFace::cacheOptimize`; `AURORA_MESH_ORDER=asset` keeps the asset's). `AURORA_RIGGED_BLEND=runs` keeps #966's drawing, `alt` alternates it. Cost (40 avatars of 8 meshes on one point, 120 fps): `g_transparent` 0.21 → 0.50 ms; one mesh each, 0.076 → 0.082 ms. Expected difference with `copy`: where an outer card is between 25 and 50 % (the top of the demo cards, seen at a grazing angle through coarse mips), the inner strands behind it show through as a blend of the two, where `copy` hides them behind any texel from 1/255 and shows the head; a threshold of 0.25 instead of 0.5 hides them too but brings back the shards of the shuffled cards and the #556 ring (tried in demo).

  - 🟡 A body add-on shows through a sheer dress in speckles ([#1300](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/issues/1300), 2026-10-28; task `rigged-blend-fringe-depth`; validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-28, the grid check left): with `Split` (#1024) a rigged blended texel under one half wrote no depth, so a mesh drawn after it and behind it (a nipple add-on worn under a knit dress whose alpha wavers around 0.5) was drawn over it there and hidden elsewhere. The Legacy Viewer hides it behind any texel from 1/255 (lldrawpoolalpha.cpp MINIMUM_ALPHA, `write_depth = rigged`). Now (`RiggedBlendDepth::Layers`, the default): object by object (`blend_order::each_object`), on a copy of the scene depth (`Targets::blend_layers`), what is half covered writing its depth as drawn, then the fainter texels, then their depth from 1/255 (`fs_depth_contact` with `DEPTH_CONTACT_ALPHA`); the scene depth takes them where half covered only (no #556 halo); one object's soft edges still hide none of its strands (no #935 shards). Choice made by the human on 2026-10-28: the Legacy Viewer's rule rather than the fringes of hair blending over a blended body drawn after it, which `split` allowed and which now show what lies behind, as in the Legacy Viewer. `AURORA_RIGGED_BLEND=split` keeps the former drawing, `alt` alternates it; demo `AURORA_DEMO_SHEER=1` (a knit dress whose alpha wavers between 0.25 and 0.75 over a red layer drawn after it): red speckles through the dress with `split`, none now, SMAA and MSAA 4x. Unchanged against `split`: `AURORA_DEMO_HAIR=8,24,60,16`, `AURORA_DEMO_HAIR_CARDS=120` (no shards), `AURORA_DEMO_HAIR_CARDS=160,layered,outer`, `AURORA_DEMO_HAIR=1,48,20` with `AURORA_DEMO_LASHES=1`, `AURORA_DEMO_HALO=1` (no ring, SMAA and MSAA 4x). Cost (crowd of 40, 60 fps cap, SMAA, alternated in one session, medians): one mesh each, `g_transparent` 0.083 → 0.131 ms; 8 meshes each, 0.521 → 0.657 ms, `gpu` +0.12 ms; one depth target of the window's size and samples more.

- 🟡 Facial expressions, hand poses, breathing and body noise of the system avatar ([#661](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/issues/661); LLEmote, LLHandMotion, LLBodyNoiseMotion, LLBreatheMotionRot, LLKeyframeMotion::onActivate / onUpdate). `scene/default_motions.rs`: the 19 expressions are built-in motions without joints, registered in the animation streamer (never fetched as assets): the simulator signals them (gestures) or an animation's `emote_name` starts one with it, unless it is already playing; it eases in 0.3 s, holds, stops itself at 1.4 s and eases out by 2.8 s, its Express_* weight following the motion's and Express_Closed_Mouth the opposite way (with several at once the strongest closes it least; the Legacy Viewer keeps the last one updated). The hand pose is the `hand_pose` of the animation of highest maximum priority (the oldest among equals, among the animations updated: see the sub-line below), its Hands_* morph blended in 0.2 s; relaxed hands without animation, as in the Legacy Viewer (they were spread). Breathing turns mChest ±0.05 rad over 2π s (MEDIUM priority); the body noise sways mTorso about a degree (Perlin noise of noise.h, HIGH priority, blended additively like LLJointStateBlender), stopped while sitting on an object or aiming. Deliberate difference: neither stops for an avatar small on screen (MIN_REQUIRED_PIXEL_AREA_*). The live morph bank (`scene/live_morphs.rs`, was `lipsync.rs`) becomes sparse, one weight column per live parameter (lip sync, body physics, 20 expressions, 13 hand poses; 64 columns in four matrices after the anchors, `PALETTE_JOINTS` 209 → 212); the vertex shader walks a vertex's entries, and skips a part at rest (a column per part says it moves); the relaxed hands are baked into the shape, the live hand weights moving from them. The demo idle animation asks for relaxed hands (it asked for spread ones), the upload window's default. Cost, two classic avatars, base and branch alternated five times (shared PC, SMAA, 120 fps cap): at rest `g_shadows_depth` 0.205 → 0.210 ms, `g_depth` 0.071 → 0.075 ms; during an expression and a fist 0.206 → 0.222 ms and 0.071 → 0.075 ms; `gpu` within noise. Demo `AURORA_DEMO_EMOTE=<expression>[,<hand pose>][,signal][,self]` with `AURORA_DEMO_CLASSIC=1`. Not done: eye blink (its own line; the bank has room for Blink_Left / Blink_Right), expressions on mesh heads (their own animations drive them).   - 🟡 Hand pose of an animation played over a stand of the same priority ([#1299](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/pull/1299)): LLMotionController::updateMotionsByType does not update a motion at full weight whose joints and priorities are all held by newer motions, so it asks for no hand pose. Aurora let every motion ask, and the older stand won among equals. `BoundAnim` keeps the joint signature (LLMotion::addJointState, `0xff >> (7 - priority)` per keyed position / rotation), and the hand pose skips the motions it does not extend. As in the Legacy Viewer, an animation without joints asks only while it eases in or out; the `AURORA_DEMO_EMOTE` animation now holds mFaceRoot at rest. - 🟡 Relief of normal maps flipped, legacy and PBR (reported on 2026-10-13 at KB: relief of the ground that looks inverted compared with Firestorm): the tangent frame taken from the screen derivatives (`perturb_normal`, common.wgsl) omitted the sign of its determinant, positive under OpenGL but negative here, where `dpdy` goes down the image; tangent and bitangent came out opposite to those of materialF.glsl / pbropaqueF.glsl, so bumps were lit like dents. The frame takes this sign. The normal map of the demo ("Normal + specular" panel, slabs of `AURORA_DEMO_PBR_OVERRIDE`) was symmetric (sin × sin) and did not show the defect: it now carries only bumps, bright on the side of the sun. Second difference, seen in the test of 2026-10-13 (marks of the ground bright where Firestorm has them dark): the frame of a legacy normal map followed its own transform (repeats, rotation), whereas Firestorm only moves its coordinates (LLFace::getGeometryVolume, xform) and keeps the tangents of the face (LLVolumeFace::createTangents); the frame now comes from the texture coordinates of the face, without transform, planar mapping or animation; PBR keeps the frame of its transform (tangent_space_transform). Verified in demo with a normal map rotated by 180°: relief flipped, like Firestorm. "Nearby objects › Describe" also logs the rotations of the maps. Third difference, the one of the reported ground (its dents stayed bright, dark in Firestorm; its normal map has neither rotation nor flip, and its specular weighs one per cent): Firestorm's ambient occlusion reads the normal of the G-buffer, normal map included (calcAmbientOcclusion, aoUtil.glsl), so a normal map relief darkens where it departs from the surface, all the more as the ambiance of the sky is strong (1.17 on this parcel); ours, computed before the lighting on depth alone, ignored it. The missing part is added to the lighting (`normal_map_occlusion`, common.wgsl: same taps, same 5 cm threshold and same settings as the pass, averaged over LL's random rotation, without noise), for legacy and PBR materials, only if ambient occlusion is enabled. Quick test on Agni on 2026-10-13 (a ground with a legacy normal map, classic sky of ambiance 1.17, low sun, SMAA): relief and dents judged consistent with Firestorm once the local lights were turned off; the bright marks that remain come from the projector lights, rendered as point lights ("Projector lights" line). Tests to complete on Agni: PBR surfaces, avatars and curved meshes; a sky of ordinary ambiance and a sky with reflection probes; a normal map rotated or flipped in its material; MSAA

- ✅ Textures: gain loading time and performance by getting out of JPEG2000 on the viewer side. The assets of Second Life stay in JPEG2000 on the server (protocol unchanged): only what the viewer does after the download can change. Today decoding goes through OpenJPEG (`openjpeg-sys`, ported from the free version of Firestorm; the official builds of Firestorm use Kakadu, proprietary and faster). Measured on 2026-10-12 (below), leads re-ranked according to the numbers.
  - ✅ measurement tools: `cargo run --release -p aurora-assets --example j2k_bench -- <cache\tex>` (decoding alone on a folder of cached textures, by size and by level, one thread then the pool); `texture load:` line of the log at the end of each load (`scene/texture_load.rs`: duration until "all loaded", decodes per level, CPU time per step, bytes downloaded, disk cache); `AURORA_DEMO_STREAM=<n>,<wave>,j2k=<folder>`: the return to a cached region replayed in demo with real J2C files. Details in docs/TESTING.md › Profiling
  - ✅ duplicate decodes fixed: an already decoded level that was waiting for its upload to the GPU was decoded again as soon as a decode slot became free (`decoded` only follows at the upload). Demo `AURORA_DEMO_STREAM=9000,9000,j2k=…`: 18,129 decodes of which 9,126 duplicates → 9,004; decode CPU time 14–21 s → 7–8 s; loaded in 3.2–5.3 s → 1.8–2.6 s (dev profile, machine shared with other builds: noisy measurements). Validated by the human on Agni on 2026-10-12 (login at Sandbox Newcomb, BackBone, Yikes, return to BackBone): all the textures display correctly. Record of this test: login, 342 textures in 9.0 s, 438 decodes, 3.8 s of CPU, 17.3 MB downloaded; BackBone (cache partly filled), 9,239 textures out of 9,251 loaded 26 s after the arrival according to the `streaming:` line, without a `texture load:` line (stays of less than 30 s, always a few downloads in progress) → progress lines every 10 s and a cut at each arrival added since
  - offline measurements (12,836 complete textures of a real cache: 3.5 GB of J2C, 13.4 Gpx, 71 GB in RGBA8 with mips; 47% in 1024, 12% in 2048 which weigh 49% of the pixels and 59% of the time; 65% with 3 components, 32% with 4): current OpenJPEG 2.5 16.9 Mpx/s per thread at full resolution, i.e. 49 ms on average for a 1024 (p95 101 ms) and 289 ms for a 2048 (p95 762 ms, worst 1.5 s), of which 93% in OpenJPEG and 7% in the conversion; one level below costs 3.4 times less; 30 threads: 291 Mpx/s, 274 textures per second; 9,000 textures of this mix at full resolution = 567 s of CPU, ~33 s on 30 threads
  - ✅ BC7 textures in video memory (lead 1, first half): texture pages in RGBA8 or in BC7 (`TexelFormat`, BC requested from the device when the card offers it), mip chains encoded by the decode task (`aurora-render/src/bc7.rs`, Intel ISPC `intel_tex_2`, "ultra fast" profile; alpha in two passes: one colour line per block, then the separate-alpha modes only if the first one damages the texture) and quality check of each level of at least 32 × 32 (blocks read back with `bcdec_rs`: the texture stays in RGBA8 if more than 1% of the checked blocks have a texel more than 16/255 away from the source, colour weighted by the alpha). Study on the real cache: the fast profile is transparent for the majority (median PSNR 53 dB) but visibly damages fine-grained normal maps and fine lattices with alpha, hence the check. Measured (`cargo run --release -p aurora-render --example bc7_check -- <cache\tex>`, 610 textures): 63% of the textures compressed, 3,425 → 1,729 MB of video memory (÷ 1.98), encoding + check = +49% of the decode time (with the check of level 0 alone: 86% compressed, ÷ 2.9, +30%). Demo `AURORA_DEMO_STREAM=9000,150,j2k=…` with GPU validation, no error; GPU test `bc7_pages_round_trip_on_the_gpu`. `AURORA_TEXTURE_BC7=0` to compare. Validated by eye by the human on Agni on 2026-10-12 (BackBone Main Store, side by side with Firestorm: boxes, can, walls "clean"; 156 to 167 fps against 119 to 148 in Firestorm). Record of this test, arrival at BackBone with the cache filled: 8,548 textures out of 8,564 displayed in 10 s, end of the loading at 33.8 s; 10,583 decodes of which 5,606 in BC7 (53%); 190 s of CPU (OpenJPEG 115, BC7 54, the rest 21). Threshold of the check: strict one kept (looser = more textures compressed, to tune by eye)
  - ✅ disk cache of the transcoded textures (lead 1, second half): `scene/texture_cache.rs`, one `cache/tex/<id>.bc7` file per compressed texture (BC7 chain of the finest decoded level, alpha class, picking mask, image header), written by a separate thread (`aurora-texcache`: written in the decode tasks, each file cost them ~15 ms). On the return, the texture is read at the wanted level and goes to the GPU without decoding, without mips and without encoding; its JPEG2000 data stays on disk as long as a finer level is not requested. Size on screen still unknown: the coarsest level first (immediate display), then the useful level. A texture that BC7 would damage leaves a file without levels: the encoding is no longer attempted. Textures kept as pixels (sculpties) or copied for the interface: always decoded. Files verified on read (sizes, length; 13 cases of damaged files tested), version in the header. Demo `AURORA_DEMO_STREAM=9000,150,j2k=…` three times in a row, GPU validation with no error: 9,651 decodes and 73 s of CPU on the first visit, then 4,283 decodes and 44 s on the return, 9,930 reads without decoding. `AURORA_TEXTURE_BC7_CACHE=0` to compare. Validated by the human on Agni on 2026-10-12 (BackBone Main Store up close, side by side with Firestorm, then after a restart of the viewer: "it looks good"; 204 fps against 175 in Firestorm). Record: first arrival at BackBone, 13,527 decodes and 265 s of CPU (OpenJPEG 156, BC7 84), 7,949 files written (858 MB); next arrival after the restart, 6,323 textures read without decoding, 7,699 decodes and 161 s of CPU (OpenJPEG 115, BC7 26), i.e. 39% less; in both cases 99.9% of the textures displayed in less than 10 s (on this 32-thread machine, the display time does not change measurably). A round trip of 20 s re-reads nothing: the textures stay 45 s in memory. After the integration of the texture memory budget (reduction on the GPU adapted to BC7 pages: the level that moves to the top must be made of whole blocks, otherwise the texture keeps its size; GPU test and demo `AURORA_TEXTURE_BUDGET_MB=150` with no error), revalidated by the human at BackBone on 2026-10-12 ("spot on"; arrival: 7,622 textures read without decoding, 151 s of CPU); the budget of their card (16.9 GB) triggers no reduction there: the one of BC7 pages is only verified in demo
  - ⬜ later, transcoded cache: the textures that the quality check keeps in RGBA8 (a quarter to a half) are still decoded on every visit, often twice (coarse level then useful level): that is most of the time remaining when coming back. A slower BC7 encoder changes almost nothing there (measured with `bc7_check`, 305 textures: 67% compressed in "ultra fast", 75% when adding "very fast" for 4 times the cost, 79% with "basic" for 19 times); still to try: their RGBA8 chain in the cache (4 times more disk, to be compressed losslessly), or a looser check threshold. Cache size to watch (858 MB for BackBone)
  - ⬜ later, BC7: better-quality encoder in compute on the GPU (crate `block_compression`, wgpu) to also compress the textures that the fast profile damages; to coordinate with the line "texture memory … then compression" (budget)
  - ✅ BC7 keeps the ends of alpha exact (2026-10-26; task `bc7-opaque-alpha`; no issue, reported by a tester: a worn hat full of 4 × 4 holes, whole with `AURORA_TEXTURE_BC7=0`). The hat's faces are legacy masks with a cutoff of 255, which the Legacy Viewer draws as `alpha < cutoff / 255` discarded (llvovolume.cpp, `mAlphaMaskCutoff`): only texels at exactly 255 show. Mode 6 shares the lowest bit of its endpoints between color and alpha; with that bit at 0 its opaque texels decode at 254, within the 16/255 tolerance of the check. Measured with `bc7_check` (which now counts the opaque texels no longer opaque) on 400 textures of the human's cache: 35 % of the opaque texels of the compressed alpha textures were lost. Every block of an alpha texture holding a texel at 0 or 255 is now decoded back: a mode 6 block gets its endpoints' lowest bits set again (color moves by 1/255 at most), the others are encoded again with alpha apart (modes 4 and 5) and their alpha endpoints and indices set from the texels' lowest and highest alpha, so that 0 and 255 come out exact; a block that still misses keeps the texture in RGBA8. Same sample after: 0 opaque texels lost, 42 % of the alpha textures compressed (47 % before, holes included), video memory 786.6 MB against 776.1 MB before (1,457 MB in RGBA8). Disk cache version 3: older `.bc7` files are encoded again on the next decode. Validated by the human on Agni on 2026-10-26: the hat is whole with BC7 on, the other see-through textures around unchanged
  - ⬜ later, lead 2: faster decoder. No free replacement: `hayro-jpeg2000` 0.4.1 (pure Rust) is on a par (19.5 against 18.7 Mpx/s) and fails on 14 textures out of 402; OpenJPEG built with `/arch:AVX2` gains ~16% (16.9 → 20.2 Mpx/s) but requires an AVX2 processor; Grok (AGPL v3, to be decided) and shared per-level decoding (not redoing the coarse levels at each step up) remain to be measured; compute decoding on the GPU: only if the rest is not enough
  - ⬜ later, measurement: the time until "everything loaded" for the same route in Firestorm (only the fps were compared)
- 🟡 Textures left white after a teleport between two busy regions (grid session of 2026-10-13: 1,822 warnings `upload refused by the renderer (slot 0, …)` for 1,532 textures in the 17 s that followed an arrival). Cause: the texture table stopped at 16,384 slots, the number of textures a shader could bind when each was an element of its own; since the pages, a slot is only an entry of the location buffer. A texture keeps its slot until 45 s after its last use, so the textures of the region left and those of the arrival region did not fit together: `TextureStreamer::acquire` gave the last ones the white texture as their slot, for as long as something used them (plain faces, opaque where the texture is transparent), and they were still downloaded and decoded, refused when sent, then decoded again at each finer level (290 of them twice). Fixed: 65,536 slots (`aurora_render::textures::SLOTS`), the pages alone bounded by what the device binds; a full table takes back at once the slots of the textures nothing uses, oldest release first, before a texture in use goes without (`TextureStreamer::new_slot`); a texture that still finds none is counted, sent nowhere and told to the log in one line for all (`texture table full …`), not one warning each. Demo: `AURORA_DEMO_TEXTURES=20000`, 3,621 white cubes and as many warnings before, none after; `AURORA_TEXTURE_SLOTS=<n>` fills the table on purpose (docs/TESTING.md). `check.ps1` green (1,874 tests passed, 24 ignored). Human trial on Agni on 2026-10-13 ("Test texture-upload-refused", a login of 89 s in a busy region, no teleport): `65536 texture slots in 16384 pages at most`, 8,884 textures at most, loading as before, neither warning in the log. The table was never full in that session: the fix itself is shown by the demo only.
  - ⬜ To verify on Agni: a teleport between two busy regions (more than 16,379 textures in the `textures=` of `perf summary` during the 45 s that follow), no white surface, neither `upload refused by the renderer` nor `texture table full` in the log.
  - ⬜ later: a texture left without a slot (more than 65,531 in use at once) stays white until nothing uses it for 45 s and it is met again, and is still decoded (sculpt maps and avatar loads wait for it). To do if it ever shows: give it a slot when one is freed, the faces that drew the white texture being told of it, and decode nothing for it meanwhile
- ⬜ Camera position at altitude, later: the camera itself stays in single precision (step of 0.24 mm in height at 2,106 m, as in Firestorm); a very slow vertical move in close-up therefore advances in notches of one pixel at most at 30 cm. Keeping the camera relative to its look-at point (or in double precision) all the way to the shader would remove them. Water and particles are still computed in region coordinates

- 🟡 HDR sky path: ACES Hill, mix 0.7, automatic exposure (task `hdr-auto-exposure`; validated by the human on Agni on 2026-10-19, side by side with the Legacy Viewer on the library Midday: brightness close, the log giving an average luminance of about 0.77 and the lowest exposure, 0.5; the legacy Midday stays at 1; reported on 2026-10-19: since the library Midday became the real non-classic sky, #498, Aurora was far brighter than the Legacy Viewer with the same preset). Skies with a reflection probe ambiance now go through the Legacy Viewer's HDR path (LLPipeline::generateLuminance / generateExposure / tonemap, luminanceF / exposureF / tonemapUtilF.glsl):
  - automatic exposure, on the GPU (`exposure.rs`, `shaders/exposure.wgsl`): one compute workgroup averages the luminance of a 256 x 256 grid over the middle 60 % of the image, nudged towards the ground, everything but the sky counted at half (RenderDiffuseLuminanceScale 0.5; the sky is told by the empty depth prepass above the horizon, where the Legacy Viewer reads G-buffer flags) plus the glow of the last frame; the exposure goes from `sqrt(gamma) x 2` in the dark to its inverse at an average of 0.5 (RenderDynamicExposureCoefficient), on a square curve, eased towards over about two seconds (RenderDynamicExposureSpeedError 0.1 / SpeedTarget 2); classic skies keep 1. The value is copied into the post uniforms by the GPU (no read back in the frame); Preferences' exposure multiplies it, and the glow, the bloom threshold and its Karis weights follow the exposed value. A photo keeps the live view's exposure. `AURORA_AUTO_EXPOSURE=0|1|alt`; the log gives `auto exposure: …` every 30 s and 4 s after a change of sky
  - ACES is Stephen Hill's fit with its input and output matrices (toneMapACES_Hill) instead of Narkowicz's, and the default tone mapper (RenderTonemapType 1 in settings.xml and every level of featuretable.txt; human decision of 2026-10-19; settings version 25 moves every earlier profile, which held the former Khronos PBR Neutral default, to it once)
  - Preferences › Graphics › Tone mapping mix (0 to 1, 0.7; RenderTonemapMix): the share of the tone mapped colour over the exposed linear one, greyed with the tone mapper on a classic sky; a classic sky tone mapped all the same (probe ambiance above 0) is not mixed (LLSettingsSky::getTonemapMix)
  - demo (`AURORA_DEMO_SKY=1,0.8,0,1`, a non-classic sky of gamma 1 like the library Midday, sunlight 2.2 to 2.7, ambient 0): average luminance 0.275, exposure 1.54, so the plaza comes out brighter than before (the Legacy Viewer's rule on a dim scene); ambient 1: luminance 0.47, exposure 0.66; the classic demo sky is unchanged (same image means, exposure 1)

    - ambient: amblit's grey luminance where the probes do not reach; the probes' irradiance comes from an irradiance capture of its own (LLReflectionMapManager's irradiance pass, RenderDesaturateIrradiance): blue_horizon and blue_density at their HSL lightness, no ambient, no clouds, drawn at 128 x 128 next to each radiance face (`probes.rs`, `probe_filter.wgsl`); with the blue sky's irradiance a white avatar came out blue
    - haze: hazeF.glsl (`ll_haze`, the additive x sky_hdr_scale and the attenuation with the distance multiplier) instead of the generic fog
    - classic skies and those with a probe ambiance of 0 are unchanged: same images in demo (`AURORA_DEMO_SKY` unset, `1,0.8` and `1,0.8,0.25,0`, mean difference 0.01 / 255)
    - demo: `AURORA_DEMO_SKY=midday` carries the library Midday's values; the white avatar and boxes in the sun come out neutral grey instead of warm beige, the scene is dim and the exposure about 1.95; `AURORA_DEMO_SKY=1,0.8,0,1` now gives an average luminance of 0.178 and an exposure of 1.81, ambient 1 0.251 and 1.61

The Legacy Viewer keeps every stage of its probes in GL_R11F_G11F_B10F (the capture, each mip, the filtered radiance and irradiance: LLReflectionMapManager, LLCubeMapArray), and the GPU truncates what is written there (measured on this PC's RTX 4090, Vulkan and DX12: every write rounded down, 6 bits of mantissa in red and green, 5 in blue): each of the nine writes down to its irradiance loses about half a step, twice as much in blue, so its ambient comes out a few percent darker and yellower than the light its probes hold. Under a sky with a probe ambiance the probe filtering now stores every stage the same way (`LEGACY_FORMAT` of `probe_filter.wgsl`: the four texels of each mip truncated, then their average), and the irradiance capture is drawn at 128 x 128 so that its chain has as many steps as the Legacy Viewer's (512, then 128 .. 2). In demo (`AURORA_DEMO_SKY=midday`) the irradiance loses 3 % in red and green and 5 to 7 % in blue; white surfaces 1.5 to 4 % darker, the shaded ones less blue; classic skies unchanged (same images, mean difference 0.03 / 255)

Not the lighting: the Legacy Viewer lights alpha-masked legacy faces exactly as the opaque ones (materialF.glsl into the G-buffer, softenLightF), and so does Aurora. The colour of the texture's mips: Aurora averaged each mip texel by the alpha of its four texels (`build_mips`), so the empty texels around the blades left no trace; the Legacy Viewer's mips are a plain average (glGenerateMipmap, LLImageBase::generateMip), and the colour creators leave in the empty texels, here a dark olive, darkens the grass seen from afar. `build_mips` now takes the plain average for every channel; the transcoded cache is version 2, so the mips of the old files are made again once. `AURORA_MIP_FILTER=weighted` brings the alpha-weighted colour back to compare. Measured in demo on a local unversioned copy of the scene (auto exposure 1.91 as on the grid): grass to floor ratio 0.072 → 0.040 in red, 0.099 → 0.055 in green, the bright yellow-green blade tips gone, as in the Legacy Viewer; on the grid the Legacy Viewer's grass is about 0.7 of Aurora's (the bed is closer there, finer mips). Every texture with transparent texels and every sky is concerned, classic ones included: distant foliage, fences and hair edges take the colour of their empty texels as in the Legacy Viewer; the alpha of the mips (coverage kept for masks) is unchanged. It also ends the lean of the normal maps' mips towards their glossy texels noted above (their alpha is the glossiness). Still to verify on Agni: other foliage side by side with the Legacy Viewer, and foliage under a classic sky (changed too); hair and fences with soft edges; the one-time re-decode of the cached textures (a busier arrival the first time)

Firestorm does the same according to its code (not observed side by side). Leads, both a deliberate difference: keep in reserve, hidden, the deleted avatars and their attachments for a few minutes, and display them again complete as soon as the simulator resends them; or only remember that an avatar has already been displayed (no more cloud, but it rebuilds in plain sight)
- 🟡 our avatar a cloud again at every teleport (reported on 2026-10-13): like Firestorm, which never destroys gAgentAvatarp (LLViewerObjectList::killObject moves it into the agent's region), our avatar is a first appearance only at login. Its loading state is kept between the region left and the next one (before: forgotten with the object of the old region, hence 2 s of attachment stability then 3 s of delay at each arrival, although textures and meshes were still in memory: 6.4 to 8.4 s of cloud in the log of a session on Agni on 2026-10-12). It is displayed as soon as it arrives, its attachments coming back one by one; the other avatars remain first appearances in the new region; the state is forgotten at logout. Merge accepted by the human on 2026-10-13 without a test on the grid (unit test: region removed then arrival in a new one). To verify on Agni: teleport to another region (avatar visible on arrival, log without a new "(own) shown after" line), walking from a region to its neighbour, cloud still present at login
- 🟡 objects kept from one region to the next, like Firestorm: an object known by its UUID keeps its slot (state, animations, linked objects, loading state of an avatar) when another region sends it (LLViewerObjectList::processObjectUpdate, LLViewerObject::setRegion; before: deleted with everything linked to it, then recreated); its linked objects follow it under their old key until their own update. Our avatar is never destroyed (killObject, process_kill_object): when the region left disappears before the destination has sent it, it moves into the agent's region with what it wears; requests to delete our attachments are ignored during a teleport or when they come from a region other than the agent's (FSExperimentalLostAttachmentsFix, FIRE-12004, enabled by default in Firestorm). After a teleport, our avatar therefore stays displayed with its attachments, instead of seeing them come back one by one. Deliberate difference: an attachment that the destination has not resent 15 s after our arrival is removed (Firestorm keeps this ghost until its next refresh of the attachments). Seated on a vehicle that crosses a border, the seat's animations are no longer stopped (the same seat under its new key). Test by the human on Agni on 2026-10-13: one teleport between regions (our avatar did not turn back into a cloud) and two border crossings in flight; merge validated. To verify on Agni: border crossing seated on a vehicle, object detached right after a teleport, attachment lost on the way (removed after 15 s, line "worn objects not sent by the region arrived in" of the log)
- 🟡 A resident seen without its attachments after a carry or pose object (#746, task `pose-invite-avatar-reset`; validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-21): when an object is deleted while an avatar sits on it, the avatar no longer leaves the world with it. Like LLViewerObject::markDead, it gets off (LLVOAvatar::getOffObject) and stays where it was drawn, with what it wears; only the seat's prims go. Before: the avatar and its attachments were removed with the seat, and the simulator, which does not send them again, only sent the avatar back when it stood it up: a system body with its bakes and nothing worn until a relog. The same for our own avatar (seat animations stopped while the seat is still known). Unit tests (seat killed with two avatars on it) and demo `AURORA_DEMO_SEAT_KILL=1`. To verify on Agni: accept a carry or pose HUD's invitation, the inviter keeps what they wear while the object is there, after it goes away and once they stand; the same seated ourselves on a temporary object that is deleted
- 🟡 avatar stuck as a cloud until the 60 s limit, reported on our avatar at login (#121): like Firestorm, what cannot arrive is no longer awaited. An invisible bake (IMG_INVISIBLE: alpha layer that hides the whole head, upper body or lower body) is a defined bake, with nothing to download (isTextureDefined, getBakedTextureImage; before: counted as "no appearance yet"); a worn mesh that the asset server does not have (404) or that is not a mesh is no longer awaited from that failure on (check_object_for_mesh_loading / isMeshAssetUnavaliable; before: only after 4 failures, never reached in 60 s), nor is a LOD that cannot be decoded or a sculpty whose texture cannot be found; a bake that nothing uses any more is no longer counted. Log: "avatar … (own) shown by the 60 s limit … still missing […]" with the state of each awaited element, and "own appearance received". Demo AURORA_DEMO_CLOUD=self: cloud for 60.0 s before, avatar displayed in 5.0 s after. Cause confirmed by the tester's log on 2026-10-11: full alpha, head, upper and lower in IMG_INVISIBLE, three "appearance" missing at each login. Test by the human on Agni on 2026-10-11 with their usual outfit (eyes and hair in IMG_INVISIBLE): our avatar displayed in 5.9 s, no regression; merge validated by the human on 2026-10-12. To verify on Agni: an outfit with full alpha (delay, and faces that use the invisible bake), a worn mesh that cannot be found

- 🟡 Projector shadows (Firestorm "Sun/Moon + Projectors", RenderShadowDetail 2, its default setting): the two projectors most present on screen (LLVOVolume::updateSpotLightPriority) have a shadow map, kept as long as they stay the priority ones; a projector that takes one sees its shadows fade in, the one that loses it sees them fade out first (LLPipeline::generateSunShadow, mShadowSpotLight). The beam, the specular reflection and the image of the projector in environment-mapped faces are shadowed, the ambiance is not (spotLightF); five taps like pcfSpotShadow, point offset by 4 cm along its normal; these shadows stop with those of the sun. The two maps occupy the fourth quarter of the cascade atlas (half their resolution), their occluders are sorted by the GPU with those of the cascades. "Projector shadows" option (on by default, no effect if shadows are off), `AURORA_PROJECTOR_SHADOWS`. Demo: post in the beam of `AURORA_DEMO_PROJECTOR`. Test by the human on Agni on 2026-10-13 next to Firestorm: the shadow of a cube placed under a projector falls at the same place; noted during that test and fixed since, the edges of the beam of a projector with a plain white texture were sharp (the fade of the edges depended on the texture's levels; it now depends only on the distance to the focal point, like getTexture2DLodDiffuse) — still to verify on Agni: these faded edges, the fade of the shadows when moving from one projector to another, the option; the shadows are sharper than Firestorm's
- 🟡 Sun shadow edges drawn as lines (reported by the human on Agni on 2026-10-16, side by side with the Legacy Viewer under the Midday sky: "hatched" shadows). Two causes in the lookup (`cascade_shadow` in `common.wgsl`), both seen in the demo's shadow view: the filter's 4 × 4 bilinear compare taps stood up to two texels apart to cover the 3 cm penumbra, and a tap only blends over one texel, so flat steps between their ramps drew several parallel edges in the two finer cascades — the same span now takes as many taps as it covers texels, at most 7 × 7 (`shadow_taps`, the same penumbra; tested across an edge in `shadow_cull`); and an object's lookup was moved off its surface along its normal-mapped normal, so the relief of the normal map printed a row of dots along the shadow edges — it now takes the face's own normal (`shadow_normal` in `object.wgsl`), as the Legacy Viewer, which moves it towards the light and so never along the relief (`sampleDirectionalShadow`, deferred/shadowUtil.glsl). Elsewhere the image is unchanged (the shadow view differs only along the shadow edges, in cascades 0 and 1). GPU, demo crowd of 40 at noon, 1683 × 900, capped at 120 fps, 3 alternated passes of 20 s: `gpu` 1.48 → 1.53 ms (within the spread of the passes). `AURORA_SHADOW_FILTER=gaps|mapped|before` brings each back, to compare. Validated by the human on Agni on 2026-10-16, side by side with the Legacy Viewer: the shadow edges are clean. Still to check on Agni: the frame rate at KB, MSAA, shadows "Ultra" and "Low"
  - 🟡 stair-stepped shadow limits on avatar backs (2026-10-17, task `shadow-stairs`; validated by the human on Agni on 2026-10-17, the stairs gone with `AURORA_SHADOW_BIAS=alt`): the receiver bias of the lookup was a fixed 0.0005 of the cascade's depth range, which is the cascade's square plus `CASCADE_DEPTH_PAD` (400 m) on each side, so about 0.4 m in the finest cascade: a point only fell in shadow behind a caster more than 0.4 m nearer the sun, and the limit where that distance crossed 0.4 m (a curved back under the shoulders, a skirt under the waist) followed the stored depth texel by texel, sharp stairs that no filter softens. The bias is now two texels of the cascade in metres along the light (`cascade_shadow`, the depth per metre read from the cascade's matrix); the normal offset (0.02 + 0.04 k m) and the slope-scaled bias of the shadow pipelines keep the acne away, as before. The Legacy Viewer biases by a fixed 0.004 of a shadow range fitted to the scene (`RenderShadowBias` -0.002 doubled in `pcfShadow`) and offsets towards the light by `RenderShadowOffset` 0.01 x 2 x (1 - N.L). `AURORA_SHADOW_BIAS=legacy|new|alt`. Demo at noon, camera behind our avatar, SMAA and MSAA with the contact shadows on: the stairs on the skirt and the shoulder blades are gone; the shadow view (`AURORA_DEBUG_SHADOWS=1`, shadow_compare.py) keeps the same share in shadow (31.2 % / 31.4 %), 0 pixel lit lost and 40 gained away from the edges, no acne on the plaza; at sunset (`AURORA_DEMO_TOD=3`) nothing changes outside our avatar. Tests: `shadow_receiver_bias_is_two_texels_along_the_light`, `shadow_bias_switch_alternates_by_the_second`.
    - ⬜ still to verify on Agni with `AURORA_SHADOW_BIAS=alt`: a low sun, flat floors and walls seen grazing (no acne), contacts of feet and objects (no detached shadows), large and tall buildings far away (the coarser cascades), side by side with the Legacy Viewer

- 🟡 Local lights that go out in front of the camera (#1032, task `light-selection`): the frame's list held the 64 lights nearest to the camera all around it within 96 m, so the worn lights of a crowd around and behind it pushed out the lights it looked at, and they came and went as it turned; switching worn lights off brought them back. The Legacy Viewer keeps 256 lights within the draw distance and draws those in the frustum (LLPipeline::calcNearbyLights, renderDeferredLighting). The list now takes the lights whose sphere reaches the view's frustum first, nearest first, then the nearest of the others; the distance is to the light's sphere (calc_light_dist), the range is the draw distance instead of 96 m, and lights without intensity, colour or reach are left out. A projector's texture is held only once its light is kept. Demo: `AURORA_DEMO_LIGHTS=150` with `AURORA_DEMO_POS="147,144"` and `AURORA_DEMO_TOD=4`: of the 101 lights that reach the view, the list held 50 and now 64, and the pools of light halfway across the ground are back.
