- 🟡 Clicks on what is rigged, and attachment menus like Firestorm (`aurora-render/src/drawn_pick.rs`, `scene/drawn.rs`, `app/click_pick.rs`, `ui/context/entries.rs`). Before: an animesh or a worn rigged mesh could be neither touched, nor selected, nor right-clicked — the right click opened the menu of whatever was behind (or the avatar's for what we wear), because the CPU search only knows a rigged mesh in its rest pose. Now the click reads what the GPU drew under its pixel: the frame that follows the click redraws the faces of the view through a camera narrowed onto that pixel (target of 2 × 2 texels: draw record, depth, surface coordinates; opaque and masked faces, then the transparent faces in front of them, where their texel is visible), with the scene's vertex shader, so posed as on screen. Nothing per frame outside a click. **Deliberate difference from Firestorm**: there a rigged mesh is only reached if `pick_rigged` is true — right click (`LLToolPie::handleRightMouseDown`) and Move tool (`LLToolCompTranslate`), plus our own rigged objects when the build window is open (`LLVOVolume::lineSegmentIntersect`); the left click and the hover pass `pick_rigged = false` (`LLToolPie::handleMouseDown` / `handleHover`, `AnimatedObjectsAllowLeftClick` commented out): one cannot touch an animesh or a worn rigged object there, the click goes to the avatar's collision volumes or to what is behind. In Aurora all the clicks reach them, where they are displayed; once designated, the object follows the rules of a prim of the same status (click action, touch, IGNORE, transparent face taken by a left click only if it acts on the object, rights, menus). Right click: rezzed animesh → object menu; object worn by us → `menu_attachment_self.xml`; by another → `menu_attachment_other.xml` (entries of the avatar then of the object), now a separate menu, in Firestorm's order: without "Offer teleport" or the complexity line of the avatar menu, with "Remove from display exceptions" only if there is one and "Save as ▸" (Backup, Collada, greyed); menu of our attachments completed ("Sit / stand", "Save as ▸", "Fly / Land" greyed when seated). The attachment of the menu is surrounded by the blue wireframe of the child prims of a selection as long as the menu is open (Firestorm: silhouette of the temporary selection). Touch of a rigged mesh: exact face, position, ST and UV (read on the GPU at the pixel), normal and binormal of the posed surface around the pixel (Firestorm sends those, unposed, of the rigged volume), zero at the edge of a face; a held touch keeps the surface of its press. Cost, crowd of 250 rigged avatars (14,562 objects, 120 fps): 0.3 to 0.5 ms of GPU in the frame of the click, nothing measurable otherwise (3.92 / 3.76 ms of GPU without a click, 3.94 / 3.75 with one click per second); the answer arrives one frame later than the depth alone (2 frames at a capped 120 fps). Demo: `AURORA_DEMO_CLICKS=150,rigged,menu|left|build` with `AURORA_DEMO_ANIMESH=1` (docs/TESTING.md): rezzed animesh, animesh worn by another, rigged mesh worn by us → 74 clicks designated out of 74 aimed in the open per kind of click (object menu, menu of an object worn by another, of our attachments; 74 touches; selection of the two rezzed animesh), point read on the GPU always within the posed bounds known to the CPU; with the old read (`AURORA_CLICK_PICK=wait`): menu of the platform or of the wall behind, no touch, no selection. First try by the human on Agni on 2026-10-12 (KB, same session as the hitch on click, 66 clicks: "perfect"), merge requested on this basis. Three selection spaces never mixed, like `LLSelectMgr::canSelectObject`: world, attachment, HUD. Position and rotation displayed, typed and sent in the frame of the attachment point (`LLPanelObject`, 3.5 m at most from the point: MAX_ATTACHMENT_DIST); in "world" grid the arrows follow this frame, hence the limb that carries the object (`LLSelectMgr::getGrid`); the object moves without the Modify right, its linked parts require it; it cannot be deleted, taken, copied, linked or sold and does not enter a selection rectangle; the objects worn by others stay unselectable. **Menus**: inventory (`LLObjectBridge::buildContextMenu`) — a worn object lists "Touch", "Edit" and "Detach from yourself" instead of Wear / Add / Attach to / Attach to HUD / Return to last location (hidden as in Firestorm, no longer greyed); outfit (`LLWearableItemsList::ContextMenu`) — "Touch" and "Edit" before "Detach". "Touch" is only active if the root of the object reacts to touch (`enable_attachment_touch`). **Inspect** (`LLFloaterInspect`, menus of objects, of our attachments and of those of others): "Inspect Objects" window with one row per prim (the linked prims indented under the root) — name, description, owner (or "[group] (group)"), creator, faces, vertices, triangles, TMem and VRAM in KB, creation date in SLT; totals on the left (objects, prims, faces, visible faces, vertices, triangles, complexity, textures, memory); sort by click on a header (ascending, descending, linkset order); columns to tick, saved (FSInspectColumnConfig, all by default); "See Owner Profile / Creator Profile" of the highlighted row; its prim outlined in yellow in the world, the others in blue. The properties come from an ObjectSelect of the prims, released on closing without touching the build selection. Deliberate differences: rows in linkset order (Firestorm stacks them in reverse), short date, texture memory estimated from their full size (Firestorm reads the GL memory when the texture is loaded), wireframe outline. Demo: `AURORA_DEMO_WORN=1|menu|edit|move|inspect` (docs/TESTING.md). check.ps1 green (1,228 viewer tests), menu / edit / move / inspect screenshots examined. Validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-13 (`AURORA_DEMO_WORN=1`, 3-minute session), not yet on the grid. Tests to do on Agni: "Edit" of a non-rigged attachment then of a rigged mesh (move, rotation, size, position kept after detaching / reattaching); attachment without the Modify right (moves, does not resize); direct click on an attachment when the build window is already open; "Touch" of a scripted object from the inventory and from Appearance › Outfit; "Inspect" on an attachment, a rezzed object and the attachment of another avatar (names, owner, creator, dates, figures), nothing left selected on closing.

Port of LLSelectMgr::pauseAssociatedAvatars (llselectmgr.cpp) with LLCharacter::requestPause and LLMotionController::pauseAllMotions: as long as an attachment is in the selection — from the right click that opens its menu, through "Edit" and the build window, until the selection is dropped (menu closed without editing, window closed, another object selected) — the avatar wearing it stands still, and a selected animated object pauses its own skeleton (an animated attachment both). The motions' clock stands still (head and eyes included); on release each motion goes on from the point it had reached, without jumping ahead; a motion the simulator stops during the pause goes at once, a new one waits for the end of the pause (stopMotionLocally: stop_immediate || mPaused). Local only: nothing is sent, the server and other viewers see the avatar as before; an import preview is never paused. HUD attachments pause nothing (SELECT_TYPE_HUD); the attachments of other avatars cannot be selected in Aurora, so they never pause anyone (the Legacy Viewer's right click selects them temporarily and pauses that avatar too). No setting in the Legacy Viewer: always on. Demo `AURORA_DEMO_WORN=freeze` (our avatar dances, right click at 700, Edit at 740, window closed at 1100); unit tests for the selection rule and the paused clock. Still to verify on Agni: a HUD attachment (no pause), the selection moved to another object while editing (the pause ends), the menu dismissed without Edit (the pause ends at once), several attachments selected together, editing while seated, an animesh rezzed in the world (it stands still while selected).

Its option `FSDisableTurningAroundWhenWalkingBackwards` was missing: Preferences › Controls › Keyboard › "Walk backward without turning around" (`walk_backwards_without_turning`, off by default as there): while the walk animation is signalled, a velocity more than 120° from the facing is drawn as a step back (`world/body.rs`), for every avatar, only on this screen. ## Interface

- ✅ Search place portals ([#1726](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/issues/1726); [PR #1734](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/pull/1734); task `search-place-portals`, follow-up to #1335 / PR #1719): drag Places and Land results, including All's Places section, into the scene in both Search layouts without adding reorder grips. Resolve the parcel asynchronously without requiring a landmark; retain Friends access by default and Shift-public on release. Full `scripts/check.ps1` green: 6,515 passed, zero failures, 32 ignored; scripts, formatting and Clippy clean. Pointer tests cover unloaded parcel details in both layouts and All, world release and Shift, while people/groups remain ordinary rows. Resolver tests cover delayed parcel/map replies, immutable arrivals, variable regions, invalid coordinates and cancellation guards. Four native French runs exited successfully; captures inspected for Search preview/public portal and History/Landmarks non-regression. Demo: `AURORA_DEMO_PORTALS=drop-search|drop-search-public|drop-search-hover`. Validated by the maintainer in the online test viewer on 2026-10-31; merge authorized.

- ✅ Places portal validation follow-up (#1335; [PR #1719](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/pull/1719); human feedback, 2026-10-31): retain reorder grips in Favorites only; restore ordinary Landmarks/History row alignment and allow every history arrival to create a portal without owning a landmark. History snapshots exact visited coordinates and uses the shared asynchronous variable-region map resolver, without inventory creation or landmark asset requests. Full `scripts/check.ps1` green: 6,506 passed, zero failures, 32 ignored; formatting, scripts and Clippy clean. Pointer regression covers sixteen views, including both History layouts and arrivals near an owned landmark; session/teleport/timeout guards verified. Native French captures inspected: Landmarks without a grip and an empty landmark inventory with a working public history portal. Both native runs exited successfully. Validated by the maintainer in the online test viewer on 2026-10-31; merge authorized. Demo: `AURORA_DEMO_PORTALS=drop-history|drop-history-public|drop-history-hover`.

- ✅ Landmark portals from Favorites and Places ([#1335](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/issues/1335); [PR #1719](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/pull/1719); task `landmark-place-portals-1335`): share landmark scene drops across all three favorite access modes and both Places layouts, retain favorite reordering, show a floating place icon/thumbnail and the portal's actual remaining lifetime. Full `scripts/check.ps1` green: 6,505 passed, zero failures, 32 ignored; scripts, formatting and Clippy clean. Pointer regression covers eleven views including wide/filtered lists, world release, Shift at release and in-list reordering; countdown and private-label regressions pass. Native French captures checked: place preview and public portal with 117 then 115 seconds remaining. Demo: `AURORA_DEMO_PORTALS=drop-places|drop-favorites|drop-favorites-public`, with `-hover` variants. Validated by the maintainer in the online test viewer on 2026-10-31; merge authorized.

- 🟡 Read-only text stays selectable and copyable (human and tester requests, 2026-10-31; task `edit-readonly-copy`): fields one may not edit were disabled egui fields, which take no pointer, so their text could not even be copied (an object's or an inventory item's name to name a folder, a parcel's media address, a gesture's trigger…). A shared widget, `widgets::text_field`, now shows them read-only in the theme's weak text colour: the text selects and Ctrl+C copies it, nothing can be typed. It replaces `add_enabled(…, TextEdit)` in the edit window (name, description), inventory properties and the notecard / animation descriptions, About Land (name, ID, media, music, auto return), the environment and day cycle editors, gestures, the scripts' dialogs, places, place details, search filters, report abuse, buy land, the texture library and the crash window. Like LLLineEditor::setReadOnly. Validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-31 (the edit window of an object they do not own, `AURORA_DEMO_ACTIONS=1`). ⬜ QA: in each, a field you cannot edit lets you select and copy its text and never takes typing; the same field, editable, still edits and saves.
- 🟡 Click to copy names in profiles (human request, 2026-10-31; task `profile-click-copy`): a left click on a resident's display name, legacy name or username in the Aurora profile, or on a group's name in the group profile, copies it; the name is underlined for a moment and a small "Copied" follows the pointer, fading out within a second (`widgets::copy_on_click`, reusable). Names that are already links (the groups listed in a profile, the founder) keep their click. ⬜ Later, if wanted: a copy for those links too (a right-click entry, or a small copy icon on hover). Validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-31. ⬜ QA: in a resident's and a group's profile on the grid, each name copies the right text; names that open something (groups list, founder) keep their click.
- ✅ Confirmed thumbnail upload feedback ([#1376](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/issues/1376), [PR #1609](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/pull/1609); human follow-up, 2026-10-30; task `folder-image-fit-1376`): keep a loading state until AIS read-back confirms the thumbnail UUID, retry only reads for propagation delays, show the actual result in the image editor and expire the inventory footer after five seconds. Full `scripts/check.ps1` green: 6,251 passed, zero failures, 31 ignored; formatting, scripts and Clippy clean. Regressions cover delayed/missing/wrong metadata, one write with bounded read retries for items/folders and removal, success/error expiry, stale replies and newer operations. Native French `image-photo-save` captures at frames 2250 and 2700 inspected: success in editor/footer, then footer cleared while the editor retains success and the snapshot window stays closed. Only the pre-existing OBS graphics-hook warning appeared in this demo. Validated by the human on 2026-10-30 in the test viewer; merge requested. No agent grid connection.

- ✅ Whole-image item and folder thumbnails ([#1376](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/issues/1376), [PR #1609](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/pull/1609); task `folder-image-fit-1376`, 2026-10-30): local image imports offer three clickable previews: the whole image scaled to a square (LLViewerTextureList::convertToUploadFile with force_square), proportional fit with transparent margins, and an initially centred crop that can be moved by dragging the image. The viewport stays within the source; releasing a drag keeps the dialog open and only an explicit click uploads the selected area. Cancel or Escape retains the previous thumbnail. Bounded background jobs prepare the previews and crop/encode the chosen JPEG2000. A full-image crop canvas with a short edge of at most 256 px stays within 4 MiB, including thin 4096 px strips; panning changes UVs without CPU resampling or texture replacement per frame. The shared modal uses three aligned columns, with no overlap. Scene snapshots and inventory texture assignment retain their existing behaviour. EN/FR/JA; demos `AURORA_DEMO_INVENTORY=image-layout|image-layout-wide|image-layout-folder|image-layout-folder-wide`. Full `check.ps1` green: 6,246 passed, zero failed, 31 ignored; scripts, formatting and Clippy clean. Regressions cover source edges, alpha, proportional margins, square/small/thin images, PNG/JPEG2000 parity, exact encoded pixels, preview clicks, aligned layout, cancellation and revoked editing permission. Actual pointer drags on items and folders verify both axes, partial and repeated movement, limits, no upload on release, and the chosen origin; lossless round-trips verify the selected crop pixels. Native French folder/portrait and English item/landscape captures inspected; the existing photo-save scenario was inspected before the panning follow-up, whose snapshot path remains covered by the full suite. Validated by the human on 2026-10-30 in the test viewer; merge requested.

- ✅ Search in the wolf menu (human request, 2026-10-29; task `menu-search`; no issue; PR [#1497](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/pull/1497); validated by the human in demo mode on 2026-10-29): a search field at the top of the Aurora menu (classic bar and islands) takes the keyboard when the menu opens; typing filters the entries of every sub-menu, listed in place under their path ("Me › Avatar health"; a path met again after one of its sub-menus gets a divider, not its heading again), a long list scrolling under the field, every word having to be in the entry's label or in the name of one of its sub-menus ("home" finds Go home and Set Home to Here). Separators and titles are hidden while filtering; a "No entry matches" line when nothing does; a click in the field leaves the menu open. Aurora's own: the Legacy Viewer's menus have no search. `menu::searchable` (`ui/menu.rs`).
  - ✅ Up / Down and Enter to pick an entry from the field (human request, 2026-10-31; task `menu-search-arrow-keys`; no issue; PR [#1752](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/pull/1752); validated by the human in demo mode on 2026-10-31): while the field filters, the first entry found is selected; Up / Down move the selection over the enabled entries found (wrapping around, scrolled into view), Enter clicks it; the pointer moving onto an entry selects it, so one row is lit at a time, and only the row lit by the keys takes Enter. The keys are taken before the field sees them, only while it has the keyboard (Tab onto its clear button leaves Enter to it); with nothing found, Enter does nothing and the field keeps the keyboard. Aurora's own, like the search. Unit test on the wrapping.
- 🟡 Advanced inventory search (no issue; PR [#1411](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/pull/1411); task `inventory-regex-filters`, 2026-10-28; validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-29): an "Advanced" mode beside quick search, in the search-in menu (Aurora) and the search-field list (Legacy style). Visual rules, never typed regex, each negatable, combined in All/Any groups. Rules compile once per change to linear-time `regex` patterns (`ui/inventory/smart.rs`) and run inside the existing parallel search; quick search keeps its code path. Fields from the Legacy Viewer's `LLInventoryFilter` (llinventoryfilter.cpp): name, description, creator and UUID (its search types), type, permissions, worn, links, coalesced objects and date (hours newer / older, since logoff). Aurora additions: the parent-folder field; the operators besides contains (is (whole word), starts with, ends with, wildcard pattern, ends in a number, has a version); Not and All/Any groups; the chip bar (Aurora toolbar); the rule builder (Filters floater); per-account saved smart searches in the sidebar (`inventory-smart-searches.json`); right-click Find similar (name stem, creator, type, folder). Demo: `AURORA_DEMO_INVENTORY=smart|aurora-smart|aurora-smart-wide`.
- ✅ Enter validates modal dialogs and their first text field takes the focus (tester report relayed by the human, 2026-10-29; task `modal-enter-focus`; no issue; [PR #1447](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/pull/1447); validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-29, no grid test needed): every `widgets::Modal` follows `LLPanel::handleKeyHere` (indra/llui/llpanel.cpp): Enter with no modifier clicks the main button (the `Primary` one, else the `Danger` one, as the Legacy Viewer's alerts default to their affirmative answer, confirmed by the human), unless a focused button clicks itself or a multi-line field writes a new line; the Enter or key repeat that opened a dialog does not answer it. Like `LLToastAlertPanel` (indra/newview/lltoastalertpanel.cpp), the first text field takes the focus with its text selected when the dialog opens; a dialog without a field takes the focus away from the windows behind. Dialogs drawn with plain buttons mark their answer with `widgets::default_button`; the media filter question keeps no default (Allow stays a click). Dialogs that already did something with Enter (search, commit) consume it with `widgets::enter_pressed`. Unit tests in `ui/widgets/modal_keys.rs`.

The window steadiness, Preferences height and inspector tests also run at 2.0×; `AURORA_DEMO_OPTIONS=2:text-size` cycles 0.8 / 1.0 / 1.4 / 2.0 / 1.0, and `AURORA_TEXT_SIZE=<size>` sets the size of one launch without saving it.

- 🟡 Resource monitor (human request, 2026-10-19; task `resource-monitor`; validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-19): the Performance window's full view is now a task-manager style monitor for power users, shown by default, a title bar button switching to the compact view (frame rate and its graph) and back; the old full view's details moved into it. A rail of eight sections, sampled every half second while the view shows, a minute of history: overview (processor, graphics card, memory, video memory, network and disk tiles, frame time breakdown, biggest consumer of each resource), subsystems (sortable table of the viewer's parts and sub-parts in seven columns, % of the machine or of one core, filter, detail pane with threads, related settings and the processor's minute), threads (per logical core load, the viewer's and the media plugins' processes, every thread group with its priority and role), memory (process, video memory against the driver's budget by kind, texture budget pressure, texture queues, GPU buffers written per frame), network (traffic, link figures, HTTP by kind, UDP throttle by channel, connected regions, busiest UDP messages), disk (reads and writes, cache by folder, hit rates, bytes by origin), scene (costliest avatars or objects, Inspect) and region (simulator health, time dilation, simulator frame). Costs are attributed from measures only (`ui/monitor/model.rs`): thread group loads (a sampler thread, `sys_probe.rs`), the frame profile and the network probes measured without a log line while the view shows, the GPU timers, disk byte counters (`disk_io.rs`); nothing measured stays a dash. CSV report into the logs folder. Demo: `AURORA_DEMO_PERF=monitor-<section>`, `monitor-scene-objects`. Performance no longer opens with the session (human request, 2026-10-19): the frame rate of the bars opens it; Preferences › General › "Performance at startup" is now the user's choice, off, instead of the window's state at exit (settings version 26 turns it off once).
  - 🟡 The monitor, `cpu summary`, `memory summary` and `off_cpu:` on Linux (task `linux-resource-monitor`, no issue; PR [#1768](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/pull/1768); validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-31): `sys_probe.rs` read the system on Windows only and gave nothing elsewhere. Linux now reads `/proc` (parsed by `sys_probe::proc_text`, unit-tested on every system with captured text): each thread's name from `/proc/self/task/<tid>/stat` and its CPU time from `schedstat` (nanoseconds; the 10 ms ticks of `stat` as a fallback), the process's from `CLOCK_PROCESS_CPUTIME_ID`, the machine's and each core's load from `/proc/stat` (idle counts `iowait`, as Windows' idle time does), the media plugins and the processes they started from `/proc/<pid>/stat` (parent, CPU time, resident memory), memory from `/proc/self/status` (working set `VmRSS`, peak `VmHWM`, private `RssAnon` + `VmSwap`: Windows' private bytes count committed memory resident or not) and page faults from `getrusage`. The kernel cuts thread names to 15 bytes: the names the monitor describes (`aurora-render-finish`, `aurora-audio-out`…) are made whole again by prefix, and a thread nobody named started by the main thread (it carries the process's name) is `unnamed`, as on Windows; one started by a named thread carries that thread's name and counts in its group (none known in the viewer's code). Aurora difference: the Priority column shows the nice value on Linux ("Nice 10" for `aurora-jobs`, lowered by `scene::jobs`), since Linux shares the cores by weight and its scale does not map onto Windows' levels. No Legacy Viewer origin: the monitor and the probes are Aurora's own. macOS still reads nothing.
  - 🟡 To check on Agni (QA testers): the processor and frame-time attribution in a busy region (KB), the media processes (parcel media, a profile's web page) with their CPU and memory, the HTTP table and the UDP messages during loading, the connected regions and their dilation, the region section's simulator statistics, the objects' names arriving, Inspect from the scene section, the CSV report, and the monitor's own cost (status bar) with the view open for several minutes.
  - ⬜ Later: memory per subsystem (needs an allocator that tracks by part; only the media processes are attributed today).
  - ✅ The `sound` and `settings` cache folders (task `cache-sound-settings-dirs`): written through `cache::write` but missing from `cache.rs` `DIRS`, so the cache never trimmed them, never counted them and "Clear cache" left them. Now managed like the others: LRU eviction, size, clearing, and two rows of the Disk section's cache by folder ("Sounds", "Environments", an eighth part colour). Their disk statistics stay under "Settings and other files". Tests: a sound evicted like a texture and counted by folder, every cache folder named in the monitor. Validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-19 (`AURORA_DEMO_PERF=monitor-disk`).

- 🟡 Windows Alt codes in every text field (human request, 2026-10-16): left Alt held, digits on the numpad, Alt released gives the character (Alt + 3 = ♥, Alt + 130 = é, Alt + 0128 = €). Windows sends it as a `WM_CHAR` after the Alt key-up, which winit 0.30 drops (it only attaches a `WM_CHAR` to the key press before it, `platform_impl/windows/keyboard.rs`), while egui-winit typed each digit held with Alt as text of its own. `alt_codes.rs` reads the sequence from the key events (`App::alt_code_key`) when egui has a text field focused: its digits are kept from the field, the character goes to egui's next frame. Windows' rules: no leading 0, the system's OEM code page with glyphs for 1 to 31 and 127 (437 in the United States, 850 in Western Europe); a leading 0, the ANSI code page (1252); numbers above 255 wrap around 256; 0, control characters and empty slots give nothing; on another system, or in the tests, 437 and 1252. Another key between the digits, or no digit, gives nothing; outside a text field Alt and the numpad keep their shortcuts; text a platform would attach to the Alt release is used instead of ours, never added to it. Unit tests of the composition and the tables, a UI test of a focused field receiving ♥ without the digit. Tried by the human with a real keyboard in demo on 2026-10-16. ⬜ upstream: winit should deliver that character (draft in the task's `.scratch/`).

A left click on the clock (system island, and the Legacy bars' clock) switches SLT and local time; its seconds can be hidden and its hours set to Auto, 12 h or 24 h (the island's right click under "Clock", Preferences › Layout › Bars: "Clock", "Clock seconds", "Clock hours"; `system_island.clock_zone`, default SLT, a saved UTC of the first version read as SLT; `clock_seconds`, default on as before; `clock_format`, default Auto). Auto follows the system's regional format, read once at startup: Windows' short time (`GetLocaleInfoEx`, `LOCALE_SSHORTTIME`), LC_TIME's T_FMT on Linux (`newlocale`, `nl_langinfo_l`), 24 hours elsewhere; 12 hours write "3:07 PM" (AM / PM from the catalogues). Local time carries its zone's abbreviation ("14:07:12 CEST", CET in winter): the system's zone read once at startup (`iana-time-zone`, which maps Windows' zones to IANA names), its abbreviation from the embedded tz database (`chrono-tz`, about 1.3 MB of the release exe: every zone, the computer's being known at run time only), worked out once a minute so a daylight saving switch shows; where the database has only numbers ("+04") or the zone is unknown, the offset ("UTC+4", "UTC+5:45"). The island's tooltip and the Legacy bars' clock tooltip give SLT and local time with how far it is from SLT ("SLT +9 h") (`ui/bars/clock.rs`). SLT now follows the US daylight saving rule of the chat transcripts (`pacific_offset_hours`) instead of a day-of-year range. Difference with the Legacy Viewer: its status bar shows SLT alone, and FSStatusBarTimeFormat defaults to the format of the viewer's language (24 hours without seconds in English, with seconds in French), with 12 / 24 hours, seconds and time zone variants (LLStatusBar::updateClockDisplay); Aurora's Auto follows the system's regional format, the user's own 12 / 24 hours choice.

What Aurora does differently from Firestorm, with the way back to Firestorm's look: Appearance (Conversations bubbles / lines `Settings::chat_style`, avatar name tags plates / classic `Settings::classic_name_tags`, look-at targets halo / crosshair `lookat::Settings::style`), Gaze ("Where your gaze goes": the point under the cursor / Firestorm's direction, new `lookat::Settings::aim`, point by default) and Avatar plates ("Expand a plate on hover", "Full plates for friends only", "Click on a plate"). "All in Firestorm version" / "All in Aurora version" set the Appearance and Gaze choices at once, not the plates' settings (`options::aurora::set_all`). The name tag style and the three plate settings left Preferences › Interface (one place per setting); no saved value moves. Behaviours that differ from Firestorm (signal of minimized windows, Voice box of the volume panel) stay where they are. Demo `AURORA_DEMO_OPTIONS=13` (`13:end` for the end of the page). To complete on Agni: with "Direction (Firestorm)", a Firestorm showing the look-at targets sees ours on the cursor's side, never on the object we hover; the four looks switched back and forth on a busy region (conversations, name tags, crosshairs of real residents).

- 🟡 **Name tags and floating texts hidden by the scene, like Firestorm** (`aurora-render/src/label_depth.rs`, `shaders/labels.wgsl`, `ui/hud.rs`). Before: the names of everyone within the name tag distance were drawn over the image, through walls, roofs and floors. Firestorm draws the name tags and the floating texts in the world with the depth test (`LLHUDNameTag::render`, `LLHUDText::render`: `LLGLDepthTest gls_depth(GL_TRUE, GL_FALSE)`): a wall hides the names behind it and cuts the one of a resident standing half behind it. Same result here, for the plates, the classic name tags and the floating texts: the visible part of a label stays, the part behind the scene is not drawn.
  - **How**: the interface marks the point of the world each label stands at (`aurora_render::world_label_at`), and what it paints for the world is drawn by a pipeline of the renderer instead of egui-wgpu's: same vertices, textures and colours, each fragment compared with the depth of the scene at its pixel. The cut is smoothed over the four depth texels around the pixel and follows the jitter of TAA (it does not shimmer). No readback, no copy of the image, no wait.
  - **Where a name tag stands**: half a metre in front of its anchor above the head, toward the camera (`ui::hud::tag_point`), so that the avatar's own head, hair or hat never cut it. Deliberate difference from Firestorm, which pulls it by the radius of the whole avatar (`LLHUDNameTag::updateVisibility`) and so shows through a wall the name of someone standing a metre behind it. The floating texts keep Firestorm's point (pulled by the radius of their object).
  - **Not hidden**: the floating texts of our HUD attachments and the tracking beacon, as in Firestorm; transparent surfaces (glass, water) hide nothing, they are not in the depth.
  - **Cost**, in front of the demo crowd (`AURORA_DEMO_CROWD=40`, `AURORA_DEMO_POS="129,134"`, 42 name plates, 229 interface meshes, capped at 120 fps), five alternated passes against `AURORA_LABEL_OCCLUSION=0`, median of the `perf summary` lines: `r_egui` 0.16 ms versus 0.12 (the labels' vertices copied with their depth); `gpu=` 0.83 ms on both sides, `u_tags` 0.08 on both sides. Consecutive meshes with the same texture and clip share a draw (the depth is in the vertices).
  - **Clicks**: a click on a name tag reaches its avatar only where the tag shows (`App::pick_name_tag` compares the depth under the cursor with the same point).
  - **Demo**: `AURORA_DEMO_TAGS=wall` (the wall in front of two residents, a floating text behind it); `AURORA_LABEL_OCCLUSION=0` draws the labels over everything, by egui-wgpu, as before. The far residents of `AURORA_DEMO_TAGS` moved out from behind the plaza's torus, which now hides what is behind it.
  - 🟡 Validated by the human on Agni on 2026-10-13 in a short session (one region, half a minute, nothing to report). To complete on Agni: a crowd under a roof seen from above (no name through the roof); a resident half behind a wall or a door frame (the name cut along the edge, without shimmer when the camera moves, in TAA too); nobody's name cut by their own head, hair or hat; names seen through a window or water; a click on a half-hidden name tag (the avatar only where the tag shows); the classic name tags and the floating texts of objects behind a wall.
  - ⬜ Later: a hidden plate still counts among the eight complete plates and the sixteen that blur the scene (`nameplate::MAX_FULL`, `MAX_GLASS`), and asks for its profile picture; a name tag pulled by the real radius of its avatar for the very large ones (a mount, a giant), whose body can cut their own name.

- 🟡 **Avatar name plates** (`ui/nameplate.rs`; mock-up chosen by the human: variant A, with the tight green halo of B) — coded, pre-validated in demo from screenshots on 2026-10-13, **not yet tried on the grid** (tests to do below). The name tag above an avatar becomes a glass plate with round ends: profile picture in a circle with a status dot, display name in semi-bold (Inter SemiBold with the embedded fonts), user name, group title, round badges floating on the upper right edge, light border and soft shadow. It is the only rounded surface of the interface (docs/BRANDING.md, AGENTS.md section 7).
  - **Three levels according to the distance to the camera** (constants of `nameplate.rs`): full plate up to 15 m, compact pill (name and badges on one line) up to 40 m, name alone beyond. A plate only changes level 1.5 m beyond a threshold and slides from one level to the other in 0.18 s (interpolated size, contents cross-faded). At most 8 full plates at a time, the nearest ones: in a crowd the following ones are compact (a full plate keeps its place as long as fewer than 10 avatars are nearer). "Name distance" and the fade beyond 40 m are those of the classic name tags. The size follows the previous one: display name at 13 points on the full plate (plate 50 points high), the rest by the proportions of the mock-up (secondary lines at 8.8 points, name at 11.1 then 9.6 points at the compact and distant levels).
  - **States, from `LLVOAvatar::idleUpdateNameTagText`** (llvoavatar.cpp): away → amber dot; do not disturb → red dot (it wins); otherwise green; blocked → plate at 62%, name dimmed in italics, forbidden badge, no dot; friend → green heart badge; typing (typing animation, never on our own plate, like FSShowTypingStateInNameTag) → badge with three animated dots; avatar too complex (shown as a silhouette) → triangle badge; in the voice channel → green microphone badge, out of it → no microphone badge (since 2026-10-14); speaking → green outline with the halo, at all levels; avatar still loading → thin bar under the text.
  - **What the classic name tag wrote, and where it went**: "(Away)" and "(Do Not Disturb)" → the dot; "(Blocked)" → the badge and the dimmed plate; complexity and surface area (options "Complexity in name tags", "Silhouettes only", "Mine too" unchanged) → one line of the full plate, or "· 245,000" after the user name when the group title takes the third line, in amber beyond the limit and in grey otherwise (Firestorm's gradient from green to red is no longer there); red struck-through microphone outside the voice channel → nothing (the human's choice of 2026-10-14, after a red badge had been tried the same day); green → orange → red outline according to the voice level → green outline and green halo that follows the level, only while the avatar speaks (human request of 2026-10-14: a silent participant has no outline, since the server does not tell whether someone's microphone is open, only their voice activity). At the compact and distant levels only the name is left (and the badges in compact): the group title, the user name and the complexity are not there.
  - **Name options unchanged** (display names, user name, "First Last" format, hide "Resident"): a hidden line is absent, never empty. A name that is too long ends with "…" at 191 points wide, on the plate only.
  - **Voice**: envelope specific to the plate (`VoiceEnvelope`: rise in 40 ms, fall in 280 ms, gate that turns the halo off in 220 ms at the end of speech); the speaking ring below (it replaced the halo of the mock-up's `.speak.thin` rule), drawn only around the plate, never under the glass; nothing in silence.
  - 🟡 **Voice states changed at the human's request (2026-10-14)**: the green outline only while the avatar speaks (the server's voice activity, `"v"` of the WebRTC data channel; it turns green and back with the halo's gate instead of switching), on every plate including ours; outside the voice channel no microphone badge at all: the red struck-through microphone first chosen that day was taken back by the human the same evening (`feat/nameplate-names-ring`), the classic name tags keep theirs. Demo `AURORA_DEMO_TAGS=voice`. Validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-14 (`AURORA_DEMO_TAGS=cycle`). To complete on Agni: a crowd (red microphone on the plates of everyone out of voice, compact pills included); in a voice parcel, the outline that appears when someone speaks and goes when they stop, without blinking between syllables; nobody's outline while silent but connected; our own plate (outline while we speak, red microphone with voice off in the preferences or on a parcel without voice).
  - 🟡 **Speaking ring (human request of 2026-10-16; validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-16 with a real microphone; to verify on Agni: other residents' levels (server "p"/128) reach amber/red only when they shout, our own plate the same as in demo)**: the halo became a ring around the plate whose gap, width, opacity and glow all grow with the smoothed level (`paint::loud_ring`, `paint::voice_light`), so the intensity reads at a glance: a whisper is a faint hairline hugging the plate with almost no glow, a normal voice a green ring a few points away over a soft glow, a shout a thick bright ring pushed out with a wide glow; it closes in on the plate as the voice starts, and is tighter around compact and far plates. The color is the microphone badge's green, sliding through `p.amber` to `p.danger` past the overdriven level like the Legacy Viewer's speaking indicator (LLVoiceClient::OVERDRIVEN_POWER_LEVEL, llvoicevisualizer.cpp, out of reach of WebRTC's levels): here a real shout, red from -18 dBFS of RMS over 300 ms to -12 (`nameplate::overdrive`, smoothed like the level), while normal speech, -30 to -24, stays green (the classic tag's -10 dBFS was never reached by a real shout). Same envelope (no flicker), palette colors only. Demo: `AURORA_DEMO_VOICE=sweep` with `AURORA_DEMO_TAGS=voice` (Tess goes whisper → normal → shout → normal every 8 s, our plate on the real microphone, whose meter is turned into the voice server's scale); `AURORA_VOICE_LEVEL_LOG=1` logs our own plate's level once a second (demo or grid).
  - **Profile pictures**: the one of the profile (`sl_image`), requested only for a full plate, at most 4 new ones per second, the nearest first (`PictureBudget`, modelled on the radar's profiles), through the path of the interface's pictures (`App::update_avatar_pics`: profile, then texture); neutral icon while waiting and for a resident without a picture; non-square image cropped at the centre; two residents with the same picture share its texture (the second one never showed).
  - ✅ **Blurred pictures (`fix/nameplate-picture-blur`, no issue; validated by the human on 2026-10-28)**: a picture first delivered from the coarse levels of a progressive download was kept for good (its texture no longer asked for), so some plates showed a blurred photo. Such interface images (profile pictures, but also group insignias and other `ui_images`) are now followed (`App::refine_ui_copies`, `TextureStreamer::refine_ui_image`): their texture keeps loading toward its UI size (256 px at most) and each finer copy replaces the pixels of the egui texture in place, for up to 5 minutes; the banner and our own login portrait follow.
  - **Setting**: Preferences › Interface › "Name tag style": Plate (default) or Classic (`Settings::classic_name_tags`); the classic name tag is drawn by the same code as before.
  - 🟡 **Names and friends changed at the human's request (2026-10-14)**: every display name in the theme's ink on the plates (it was light violet for a friend, pink for Linden Lab staff, dimmed for a blocked resident); Preferences › Colors › "Color the names by relation" (`ColorSettings::relation_names`, off by default) colours them again, on the plates and the classic tags alike, with the colours of that page (me, friends, blocked, Linden Lab) — Firestorm always colours them (`LLVOAvatar::getNameTagColor`), a deliberate difference. The match / mismatch pair stays the classic tags' own. A friend's heart badge is green (`heart-filled`, `success`; it was light violet); a violet ring around a friend's picture was tried the same day and dropped by the human; the status dot is unchanged (present, away, do not disturb). Settings from before the switch keep the colours by relation on if the classic tags were the style.
  - 🟡 **Full plates for friends only** (human request of 2026-10-14): Preferences › Interface › "Full plates for friends only" (`Settings::plates_friends_only_full`, off by default; shown with the plate style only): a resident who is not a friend stops at the compact pill however near, our own plate stays complete (confirmed by the human), the far pill still follows the distance (`nameplate::friends_level`). Not in Firestorm. Demo `AURORA_DEMO_FRIEND_PLATES=1`. Validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-14 (`AURORA_DEMO_TAGS=cycle`), with the names, the green heart and the voice badges above. To complete on Agni: a crowd (white names, no microphone badge outside voice, the option on and off), real friends (green heart; with the colours by relation on, their name colour on the plates and the classic tags), and an existing profile from before (colours by relation on only if the classic tags were the style).
  - 🟡 **Plate interactions** (human requests of 2026-10-14; not in Firestorm, where a click on a name tag is a click on its avatar): Preferences › Interface › "Expand a plate on hover" (`Settings::plates_hover_expand`, **on** by default): the plate under the pointer shows full whatever its distance, the crowd or "full plates for friends only", and stays so 0.3 s after the pointer leaves (`nameplate::hover_level`, `HOVER_LINGER`); not over a window, while the camera or a drag holds the mouse, nor in mouselook. "Click on a plate" (`Settings::plate_click`: nothing by default, view profile, send IM, offer teleport, open the avatar menu — entries of the avatar's menu): over another avatar's plate the pointer becomes the hand of a clickable object, and a left click without Alt / Ctrl / Shift runs the action instead of reaching the world (`app/plate_click.rs`); the right click, Alt camera, HUDs and our own plate are unchanged. Demo `AURORA_DEMO_PLATE_HOVER=x,y[,click]`, `AURORA_DEMO_PLATE_CLICK`. Validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-14 (hover on pills and far names, with and without "full plates for friends only"; the four click actions and the hand cursor). To complete on Agni: hover and click in a crowd, the click actions on real residents, the Alt camera and HUD clicks over plates.
    - ⬜ Later: hover tests the plate's rectangle only, not the scene's depth (a plate hidden behind a wall can grow when the pointer passes over where it stands; the click does test the depth); more click actions already in the avatar's menu could be offered (Add friend, Teleport to avatar, Pay).
    - ✅ Hover feedback ([#473](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/issues/473); task `nameplate-hover-feedback`; validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-21): the plate under the pointer answers even when it is already full and whatever "Expand a plate on hover" says: its surface goes 12% toward the ink and its border gains 0.18 opacity, eased in and out over 0.12 s (`HOVER_LIGHT`, `HOVER_BORDER`, `HOVER_EASE`); when the pointer reaches it, its surface alone bounces (a 0.36 s damped spring, about 2 points out, half a point in, `bounce_grow`), the text and picture stay put and sharp and the pointer's rectangle does not move. "Reduce animations" keeps the light and drops the bounce. Not in the Legacy Viewer.
  - **Deliberate difference from Firestorm, requested by the human: colours fixed by the theme.** The plates do not read the name tag colours of the preferences (configurable in Firestorm): name in `ink` (ours too), `violet_light` for a friend, `rose` for Linden Lab staff, `muted_dim` in italics for a blocked resident; user name `muted`, group title `teal`. These settings now only serve the classic name tags: on the Colors page their group is greyed out (without disappearing) with the note "Used by the classic name tags." as long as the Plate style is chosen; the minimap markers and the chat colours stay active. What the plate no longer shows: the "My name" colour, and the "Matches / Non-matches" distinction (two identical colours by default).
  - **Other differences, from Firestorm or from the mock-up**: typing is always shown (FSShowTypingStateInNameTag is off by default in Firestorm); the scene blur is darkened by 35% under the tint (`GLASS_SHADE`), without which the plate turns light grey on a white wall or a bright sky and its grey lines get lost in it; the badges are 90% opaque instead of 72% (they have no blur of their own, the plate's border would show through); no saturation of the blur (the windows' one, shared, as is); filled Tabler icons (microphone, heart, triangle, forbidden) instead of the mock-up's outline icons; blur reserved for the 16 nearest plates (full or compact), denser tint for the others and for the distant pills.
  - **Drawing and cost**: the geometry of a plate (pill, border, shadow, halo, picture ring, status dot, badge discs) is made of simple meshes (`nameplate/mesh.rs`) instead of egui's rounded shapes, kept as long as the avatar's state does not change, moved on every frame and redrawn without a copy when the plate has not moved (`nameplate/paint.rs`). Measurement: demo `AURORA_DEMO_CROWD=40` (41 name tags), dev build, cap at 120 fps, the two styles alternated every second in the same session (`AURORA_NAME_TAGS=alt`), medians of the 30 seconds of plates and of the 15 seconds of classic name tags of each pass, PC shared with other agents.
    - in the crowd (`AURORA_DEMO_POS=135,134`), camera still, 3 passes: `u_tags` 0.06 ms versus 0.05; `r_tessellate` 0.16 versus 0.14 to 0.15; `r_egui` 0.12 versus 0.09; 165 egui meshes versus 195; 18,000 vertices versus 13,200;
    - in front of the crowd (`129,134`), 2 passes: `u_tags` 0.08 versus 0.06; `r_tessellate` 0.16 to 0.17 versus 0.14 to 0.15; `r_egui` 0.12 versus 0.09; 162 meshes versus 195;
    - geometry copied again on every frame (upper bound of a moving camera, forced for the measurement), 2 passes: `u_tags` 0.11 versus 0.06;
    - worst frame: frame `max` identical (8.35 to 8.43 ms at the cap); `r_tessellate` exceeded 1 ms in 2 seconds out of 210 with the plates (1.14 and 1.24 ms), never in the 105 seconds of classic name tags;
    - first version, with egui's shapes and no limit on full plates: `u_tags` 0.22 ms, `r_tessellate` 0.33, 39,300 vertices.
  - **Demo**: `AURORA_DEMO_TAGS=voice|status|cycle` (nine residents in all the states, at the three distances, generated pictures, white wall behind two of them); `AURORA_NAME_TAGS=classic|plate|alt` to force a style or alternate during a measurement (docs/TESTING.md).
  - 🟡 To validate on Agni: real profile pictures (arrival delay, round cropping, residents without a picture); halo on real voice levels (amplitude, no flicker); legibility in a real crowd (thresholds of 15 and 40 m, limit of 8 full plates) and on a bright sky; away, do not disturb and typing of real residents; friends, blocked residents, Linden staff; names with extended characters in semi-bold (they go through the system fonts, in normal weight); right and left clicks on a plate; `u_tags`, `r_tessellate` and `r_egui` in a busy place.

- 🟡 **"Search" window (Firestorm's legacy search, Ctrl+F and button of the bottom bar)**: port of FSFloaterSearch and its panels (`fsfloatersearch.cpp`, `floater_fs_search.xml`, `panel_fs_search_legacy_*.xml`, flags of `llqueryflags.h`, `llclassifiedflags.cpp`, `lleventflags.h`, content access of `llagentaccess.cpp`). Tabs in the order of `floater_fs_search.xml`: Web, People, Groups, Places, Land Sales, Events, Classifieds; the window opens on the last tab used (FSLastSearchTab, 0 = Web the first time). Network (`aurora-net/src/search.rs`, `session_search.rs`): DirFindQuery (people, groups, events "u|category|text" or "day|category|text"), DirPlacesQuery (sorted by traffic), DirLandQuery, DirClassifiedQuery, sent reliably with the flags of `find()`; replies DirPeopleReply / DirGroupsReply / DirPlacesReply / DirEventsReply / DirClassifiedReply over UDP and DirLandReply through the event queue (with ProductSKU), ignored if they name another agent; details by AvatarProperties (AgentProfile capability, otherwise UDP), GroupProfileRequest, ParcelInfoRequest, ClassifiedInfoRequest, EventInfoRequest; land types by ProductInfoRequest. Model (`world/search.rs`): one list per tab, query identifier (a reply to an older query is ignored), pages of 100 (the row beyond announces the next page: "> 100 found"), status codes (banned word, terms too short, nothing found, search disabled, and those of the events), words of 2 letters or fewer removed (`filterShortWords`), UUID key typed in People resolved by the name cache, filters reapplied on the viewer side (price / area of the land, maturity rating of the events), first row selected and its details requested. Window (`ui/search.rs`, `ui/search/details.rs`): form of each tab (Firestorm's categories, G / M / A checkboxes, General / Moderate / Adult level of the groups, price ≤ and area ≥, sale type, server sort and ascending order, "Ongoing and Upcoming" or date with previous day / next day / today), list with sortable headers, counter, previous / next pages, details on the right with their actions (profile, IM, teleport offer, friend, block, map, name menu; group chat, copy of the URI and of the name; place profile of "Places" with Teleport, Map, Copy SLurl; classified sheet; event sheet with clickable organiser and place). Firestorm's default values: General content only (ShowPG* = 1), General groups (FSSearchGroupMaturity = 13), land sales like `FSPanelSearchLand::find`: "Price ≤" checkbox ticked and "Area ≥" checkbox unticked (FindLandPrice = 1, FindLandArea = 0), price field showing "0" and area field empty (the local source leaves `edit_price` empty, the released Firestorm shows 0 there; the query is the same, 0, and the 0 makes visible what is sent; an emptied field still counts as 0), type "All Categories" selected (FindLandType), sorted by name; DFQ_LIMIT_BY_PRICE / DFQ_LIMIT_BY_AREA follow the checkboxes, both values are always sent (0 for an empty field) and the viewer filters the replies again (price > limit or area < limit discarded): by default only the rows at 0 L$ remain, that is the auctions, displayed at 1.0 L$/m² as in Firestorm, the window closes after a teleport (FSLegacySearchActionOnTeleport = 1), last tab remembered (FSLastSearchTab). Deliberate differences: the M and A checkboxes are greyed out with an explanation when the account or the content preference does not give access to them (Firestorm leaves them tickable without sending them); next / previous page replays the query of the displayed page, even if the field was changed in the meantime; no drop-down history of searches. Web tab: the grid's search page in the built-in browser (CEF, `ui/web_view.rs`) with back, forward, reload, search page, editable address and "Open in browser"; the page is opened with the session, like Firestorm (`FSPanelSearchWeb::loadURL`, `LLWeb::expandURLSubstitutions`, `LLViewerMedia::getOpenIDCookie`): the address is Firestorm's `SearchURL` with `sid=<session id>` (the `[TYPE][COLLECTION]` tokens stay as they are in it and `&maturity=g|gm|gma&` is added, as its panel does), and the OpenID cookie of the login is given to the browser before the first page (it only goes to its own domain). The session identifier is only put in a `https://search.secondlife.com` address built by the viewer, is never logged or saved by Aurora, does not appear in the address field and "Open in browser" opens the address without it; the browser and its page are dropped on logout; nothing is sent in demo. The browser of this tab has its own profile (`media/private_profile.rs`): as the CEF plugin has no in-memory mode (it always gives CEF `<cache_path>cef_cache/<pid>` and a log file), its cache, its history, its local storage and its `cef.log` go into `cache\web-private\<pid>-<n>\`, **deleted after use** (closing the window, logout, exit of the viewer, and a sweep at the next start of what a crash left behind; a lock protects the profile of another running viewer); nothing of this page goes into the shared cache `cache\cef` nor into `cache\cef.log`. While the browser is running, these files exist on the disk. Deliberate differences: the page is only loaded when the Web tab is displayed (Firestorm loads it every time the window is opened); on the beta grid (human request) nothing of the session is sent — neither `sid` nor OpenID cookie —, the page of `search.secondlife.com` is opened anonymously there with the note "Web search is anonymous on this grid.", whereas Firestorm sends the beta's session identifier to the main grid's site. Demo: `AURORA_DEMO_SEARCH=<tab>[:text]`, `AURORA_DEMO_SEARCH_WEB=<page>`; unit tests of the flags, messages, replies, pages, statuses and replies of the demo. **Nothing has been tried on the grid.**
  - **Shared theme**: the window passes the theme guard (`ui/theme_guard.rs`) with no exception or marker. G / M / A, "Price ≤", "Area ≥" and "Ascending" checkboxes through `widgets::checkbox`, "Ongoing and Upcoming" / "By Date" through `widgets::radio_value`, text only measured in `Color32::PLACEHOLDER`; sortable header, sort arrow and row highlight like the radar (`ui/people/radar.rs`); "More" menus through the rows of `ui/menu.rs`. The guard now also recognises an egui checkbox written on its own line of a call chain (`.checkbox(`) or without a label (`egui::Checkbox::without_text`), which it used to let through.
  - **Ctrl+F, a single rule** (`ui/find_shortcut.rs`, function `owner`, tested): three functions ask for it — the search of the script editor, the search bar of a conversation (Conversations and History windows) and "Search". 1) The keyboard is in a field: the window of that field wins (script editor, conversation), wherever the pointer is; 2) the keyboard is nowhere: the conversation under the pointer; 3) otherwise — nothing selected and pointer elsewhere, or keyboard in another field (chat bar, filter, field of "Search") — the viewer's shortcut on these keys, "Search" by default, like the accelerator of Firestorm's menu. The same rule is read by the window when it draws itself and by the application before launching its shortcut: never both, never neither. The shortcut of "Search" remains editable in the preferences; placed on other keys, it no longer yields anything.
  - **Windows**: `widgets::Floater`, so placed by a `Slot` of the layout like the others (follows the edges of the viewer's window, snaps to the other windows and to the work area, moves as a block with its neighbours); closed at the first launch; opened in the middle of the work area (`search::default_rect`, 900 × 600, minimum 720 × 440; Firestorm: 780 × 590, centred), away from the bars. At 1280 × 720 it lands at (190, 57) and leaves visible 182 px of the radar on the left and of Performance and Conversations on the right, the minimap almost whole (test `the_first_launch_windows_take_their_corners`).

Also: Ctrl+F on the real keyboard (keyboard in the field of a conversation or pointer over Conversations: search bar alone; pointer over the world or keyboard in the chat bar: Search; script editor: its search); `cache\web-private` folder empty after the Web tab is closed; on the beta grid, page opened anonymously.

- ✅ **Extended characters in names, titles and messages (#127)**: a character absent from the embedded fonts was drawn as a square everywhere Aurora writes text (avatar name tags, hover text, chat and its lists, profiles, input fields: a single text path, egui). The report shows a group title surrounded by "ღ" (Georgian, U+10E6); also missing were Armenian, Hebrew, Arabic, Japanese, Korean, Chinese, the Indic scripts, Thai, the mathematical letters of "fancy" names (bold, script, fraktur, double-struck), circled letters, arrows, box drawing and blocks, braille… These characters now come from the fonts installed on the system, as in Firestorm (`fonts.xml`, `<os name="Windows">` added to each font, looked up by `LLFontRegistry::createFont` in `LLFontGL::getFontPathSystem`; Firestorm additionally embeds DejaVu Sans, which draws its "ღ"). Aurora's own list: one Windows 10 / 11 font per script (Segoe UI, Segoe UI Symbol, Meiryo or Yu Gothic, Malgun Gothic, Microsoft YaHei and JhengHei, Nirmala UI, Leelawadee UI, Ebrima, Gadugi, Microsoft Himalaya, Javanese Text, Segoe UI Historic, SimSun-ExtB, Segoe UI Emoji for recent emojis in monochrome…), Japanese before Korean and Chinese like Firestorm, the first font present that has the probe character being kept. They come after all the embedded fonts, in both families: what was already drawn does not change. Files memory-mapped without a copy (no weight added to the package, no new dependency), looked up and checked on a separate thread from launch, installed on the next frame if they were not ready; baseline of the fallback fonts aligned with that of the main font (egui centres their line, which raised Japanese by a quarter of the font size). Module `ui/fonts/fallback.rs`. Demo: `AURORA_DEMO_GLYPHS=1` (or `2`), comparison with `AURORA_FONT_FALLBACK=0`. Measurements (dev profile, this PC): lookup 1.3 ms off the main thread; construction of egui's fonts 1.3 ms instead of 0.2 to 0.4 ms, once; `ui` step unchanged (0.35 to 0.44 ms before and after); about 2.5 MB of resident memory at launch, 6 MB after displaying all the scripts of the demo. Verified in demo on Windows 11. Defect found at the human validation of 2026-10-11, also present on main: `ui::layout::load` replaces egui's memory, where the fonts installed just before are waiting; any session with a saved layout (so outside screenshots) started with egui's fonts, without the font chosen in Preferences or the fallback fonts. The fonts are now installed after the layout (`App::new`), test of the order in `ui/layout.rs`. `check.ps1` green (1,095 tests passed, 13 ignored). Validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-11, in a normal session with their saved layout.

  - ⬜ later: right-to-left word order (bidi algorithm, absent from egui 0.36) and cursor / selection in these texts; combining marks taken from a font other than that of their base letter, which egui does not draw ("᭄" after Latin letters); colour emojis in name tags, lists and fields (Noto 3D only in messages); macOS and Linux font lists written but never tried (Windows releases only); embedded fallback font (DejaVu Sans like Firestorm, about 750 KB) if a system without these fonts has to be supported
  - ⬜ later, when egui is fixed (defect of egui 0.36.2, [emilk/egui#8576](https://github.com/emilk/egui/issues/8576), still present on its `main` branch; no fixed version as of 2026-10-12; egui 0.37.0 shapes mixed runs right ("a אבג b": 7 glyphs) and Ctrl+← from the end of "Aurora بღd" works, but an Arabic-only run still has surplus glyphs, "بب": 3): previous word in a field that contains letters written from right to left. Cause: a run that starts with a right-to-left letter and has n characters comes back from shaping with 2n − 1 glyphs ("بب": 3 glyphs), whatever the fonts, whereas all of egui's cursor code counts one glyph per character. The end of the line therefore goes past the text, and the "previous word" (`ccursor_previous_word`) subtracts below zero: Ctrl+← sends the cursor back to the start of the text, Ctrl+Backspace and Ctrl+W erase everything before the cursor instead of one word, a double-click after the last word of a field selects from the start (published and development builds); the "Debug" viewer and the `ci` profile (overflow checks) stop. No reliable workaround in Aurora alone: the number of glyphs is set in `epaint`, with no hook, and the viewer has about 75 input fields. The human's choice on 2026-10-12: wait for the upstream fix rather than embed a fork of egui; a fix in two small pieces (`epaint` and `egui`) was verified on a copy of egui 0.36.2 with `cargo test --profile ci` and proposed upstream ([emilk/egui#8698](https://github.com/emilk/egui/pull/8698), as a draft, to be reviewed by the human before marking it ready). Tests in `ui/fonts.rs`: `egui_still_shapes_surplus_glyphs_in_right_to_left_runs` fails as soon as a version of egui fixes the defect; the two `#[ignore]` tests that follow it will then have to be re-enabled, Ctrl+← and Ctrl+Backspace put back in `fallback_text_survives_selection_and_editing`, and the chat field and the script editor checked in demo
- 🟡 **Right-to-left text in reading order (bidi)** (human request of 2026-10-27): Arabic and Hebrew sentences were drawn with their words from left to right (egui 0.37 has no bidi algorithm; its shaper only reverses each run of one font), Arabic-Indic digits reversed. Module `ui/bidi.rs`: the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm (`unicode-bidi`, mirrored brackets with `unicode-bidi-mirroring`) on top of egui's layout. A text that holds a right-to-left letter or an Arabic-Indic digit is broken into rows first (own line breaking, `max_rows` and the overflow character kept: the end in reading order is cut), each row is put in display order (rules L1, L2, L4), and egui gets it with each right-to-left word in its own section in reading order (the shaper reverses and joins it) and each other right-to-left character alone; `Visual` keeps the box of every character of the original text for links, badges and selection. Other texts go through egui unchanged. Applied to the name tags and plates (names, titles), object and HUD floating text, chat bubbles above the avatars, the chat bar and its cards, and the Conversations transcript, where a message read from the right flows from the right edge (pieces, links and emoji pictures in reading order) and keeps drag-selection and copy in reading order. A chat line that starts with its sender's name stays left to right, the name isolated as between FSI and PDI (`Base::Sender`): it stays first, after its picture, and an Arabic message follows in its own order. The one-line labels cut with an ellipsis (`widgets::elided_label`, `paint_elided`: message headers, lists, tabs) go through `ui/bidi.rs` too, cut at their end in reading order, whole in their tooltip. Each character keeps its own direction for the cursor and the selection (Latin words in a Hebrew line), selected right-to-left text takes the selected text colour, and painting alone (name tags, floating text) skips the characters' boxes. Going beyond the Legacy Viewer, which has neither shaping nor bidi. Demo: `AURORA_DEMO_GLYPHS=rtl`, `rtl2` (with `AURORA_DEMO_BARS=legacy AURORA_DEMO_CHAT_LINES=legacy`: the lines above the chat bar with their pictures). PR #1191, maintainer review addressed. Validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-27 (Linux); to verify on Agni with real names and chat.

Nothing is read or written before the account is known; on logout the folder closes, the conversations, nearby chat and history windows in memory are emptied (deliberate difference: nearby chat stayed displayed from one account to the next), and the lines already queued keep the path of the account that wrote them. The history of a group's chat server has its own tint (`ChatHistoryMessageFromServerLog`) and does not repeat what the file already contains (`addMessagesFromServerHistory`: older than the end of the file ignored, same minute compared by the text; written to the file when the chat was opened by us). Exceptions, all with their reason and all verified: 7 file entries (`ALLOWED`: shared windows, maps, brand sky, debug lines, voice ring, builder of the right-click menus) and 8 `// theme-guard: content — reason` comments for 14 content lines (image tint, rating, parcel legend, white texture, sheen of the loading banner, complexity colours on the classic name tag, values taken over from Firestorm). `ui/hud.rs` no longer has an exception since the name plates were merged: the classic name tag takes the theme's card radius and `widgets::TRACK_RADIUS` for its loading bar, with no visible change; the name plates (`ui/nameplate.rs`) only read palette roles; a comment alone on its line covers the following lines that need it, and a comment that has become useless makes the test fail. `ui/chat.rs` no longer has an exception since the conversation history was merged: the pills of its toolbar buttons and the initials squares take the theme's card radius, the profile pictures `widgets::PICTURE_TINT`, and the entries of the conversation list are square like the rows of the Contacts tab (their selection bar runs along the left edge); the conversation view, the search bar, the History window and the preferences rows already wrote only palette roles (history grey: `muted_dim`, background of the matches: `amber`).
    - ⬜ later: egui's `DragValue`; "group", "others", "public" labels of the parcel legend (Land tool) to pass through `tr!`; `danger` / `amber` faces: text in `navy`, to be decided whether a dedicated role is wanted.

The theme guard fails on a window that sets its own scroll style (`ScrollStyle`, `spacing_mut().scroll`), except in `ui/widgets.rs`, and a test checks the theme's bars do not float. The lists whose rows were sized outside their scroll area leave the strip too (group members, Contacts tabs, land scripts and access lists, conversation list, profile lists and text areas, login accounts and carousel, Firestorm-style notifications, notecard editor, shape previews; the outfit gallery keeps its columns), and the table headers above a list (blocked list, radar table, search results, inspect) follow the bar the list shows (`widgets::header_width`). Limits: a content-sized window whose body starts to scroll (taller than the screen) grows 10 px wider for the bar; a table header follows its list's bar one frame late when the bar appears or goes.
    - ⬜ To check on Agni: long real lists (a large group's members, many friends, a long Contacts / conversation list): no row clipped at the right, the bar over nothing.
  - 🟡 Preferences, long labels: a label wider than its column ("Report a bug in the top bar", which its switch used to cover) continues on a second line; the settings column does not move and only that row grows, in French as in English and whatever the font size (`row_label` in `ui/options.rs`, for the setting rows and the shortcut rows). Verified with screenshots in both languages; does not depend on the grid, to be looked at once in the viewer.
  - 🟡 Windows keep their edge when the viewer window changes size (human request of 2026-10-12: the minimap did not stay at the top right; `ui/layout.rs`): egui remembers the top-left corner of a window, so a layout made in a small window left the minimap in the middle of a large one. Each window now keeps its distance to the nearest left or right edge, and to the nearest top or bottom edge, as Firestorm's floaters follow the edge they are closest to (LLFloaterView::reshape): the minimap and Performance stay at the top right, what is on the left stays on the left, what is at the bottom follows the bottom; at equal distance (centred window), it stays with the left edge and the top edge. Applies during a resize, between two sessions (the position and the screen of each window are saved with the layout: a layout made at 1280 × 720 opens correctly at 1600 × 900) and for a window reopened after a size change. All `widgets::Floater` windows and the minimap; menus, tooltips, notifications and the login screen, which compute their place every frame, are not concerned. An unusable screen (less than 320 × 240) is ignored. A window left smaller than its default size also gets its place back at startup: egui measures it on its first frame and then keeps it within the screen as if it had its default size, which pushed it away from the bottom and right edges (Conversations at the bottom right); the next frame puts it back where it was. For screenshots: `AURORA_CAPTURE_LAYOUT=1` makes the saved layout be read again. Limit: a layout saved before this change does not know its original screen; a window already misplaced stays there until it is moved once (or "Reset everything"). **To be tested by the human (does not depend on the grid):** resize and maximise the viewer window with the mouse, change screen or resolution, reopen a window after a size change.
  - 🟡 Snapping windows (human requests of 2026-10-12; `ui/snap.rs`, `ui/layout/gesture.rs`; Firestorm: LLView::findSnapRect / findSnapEdge, SnapEnabled, SnapMargin = 10 px, dependent floaters): a window moved by its title (the minimap: by its whole surface) to less than 10 px from the facing edge of another open window, of the top bar, of the bottom bar or of a screen edge sticks to it; next to a neighbour, its edges on the same side also align (top with top, etc.). Each axis chooses the nearest snap. It follows the pointer without jumping: a violet guide shows the edges that are going to touch or align and the outline of the place where it will land, and the snap happens on release; the guide does not flicker (the displayed snap holds 4 px beyond the margin, a neighbour must be clearly closer to replace it). **Resizing**: the dragged edge or edges snap to the same targets, under the pointer (the window is laid out again at each size and its content can refuse one: snapping on release would have caused a jump); a snap that would go below the minimum size is not offered. **Snapped windows**: two windows placed side by side by a snap (not by a mere alignment) stay together: dragging one moves the whole group, as one block, kept whole within the screen and snapped like a single window (each member against the other windows, the outline of the block against the bars and the edges); the group is saved with the layout and follows, as a block, the nearest edge when the viewer window changes size. A window leaves its group when it is closed, when it is collapsed, when the common edge is pulled apart by resizing it, or when it is dragged with **Alt**; Alt during a gesture also prevents any snap. During the gesture, a pill near the window is a reminder of it: Alt key then "do not snap" (snap offered) or "detach this window" (group), after 150 ms. Snapped windows touch, edge to edge, each other as well as the bars and the edges, like Firestorm's floaters (see the "no gap" sub-line). Aurora choices compared with Firestorm: a window attracts another one only if they would share a stretch of edge, guide and snap on release, groups for all windows. "Snap windows" setting (Preferences › Interface, enabled; `snap_windows`). All `widgets::Floater` windows and the minimap, which switches to the same resize handles as the others (`widgets::bare_window`). Demo: `AURORA_DEMO_SNAP=1|groupe|taille`. **To be tested by the human (does not depend on the grid):** the real mouse gestures, verified so far by tests and by the scripted demo only — move a window near another one, near the bars and the edges, drag an edge towards a target, move a snapped group, Alt during the gesture, move and resize the minimap.
    - ✅ Snapping with no gap (human requests of 2026-10-13, validated by the human in demo the same day; `layout::GAP` goes from 8 to 0): snapped windows kept a gap of 8 px between them, and with the bars and the edges; they now touch, edge to edge, as in Firestorm (findSnapRect is called without `padding`). The first-launch layout follows the same gap, so its four windows are also placed against the bars, the edges and their neighbour (Performance touches the minimap; at 1280 × 720, Conversations opens 284 px high instead of 252). Limit: a saved layout keeps its positions, and two windows snapped at 8 px by a previous version stay where they are but no longer form a group; snapping them again is enough (or "Reset everything").
    - ⬜ later: resizing the common edge of two snapped windows moves only that edge (the link is then removed); a splitter behaviour (the neighbour grows or shrinks by the same amount) remains to be done. No permanent marker on snapped edges. A window dragged into the top bar is not brought back below it.
  - ✅ Resize corner in the Aurora theme (human's choice of 2026-10-14, variant A of the mock-up, validated by the human in demo the same day; `ui/widgets/resize.rs`): the three grey hatch lines, drawn over the rounded corner and without any state, become an arc of the window frame around the bottom-right corner (2 px, `muted_dim`, the theme's inner radius), longer and in `violet_light` when hovered or dragged; the edges that move light up in `violet_light` along the frame (faded in); grab areas of 16 px inside + 4 px outside at the corners (was 10 + 10) and 4 + 3 px on the sides (was 3 + 3; Firestorm: 11 px handle, 3 px bars). Same on the floaters, the minimap and the map; system cursors kept. Demo: `AURORA_DEMO_RESIZE=corner|edge|drag[,<window>]`.
- 🟡 Frame rate and screens with different refresh rates (#120: without sync or limit, 600+ fps on one screen and 144 on the other, a 144 Hz variable refresh rate one). The reported cap is not reproduced (test machine: two identical 165 Hz screens) and its cause is not demonstrated: in world, without a limit, Aurora waits only for the swapchain. Two defects established from the code are fixed; verified in demo on two identical screens (forced mode, window moved from one screen to the other), merge requested by the human on 2026-10-12 without a trial on their part. Toggling sync during a session verified in demo (`FifoRelaxed` at 165 fps, then `Mailbox`). To verify: two screens with different refresh rates:
  - screen refresh rate read only once when the window was created, hence that of the launch screen: it now follows the window and the screen's current mode, re-read once per second (`screen_rate.rs`, a few microseconds; change logged). It bounds the login screen and decides whether vertical sync already paces the frames (with the old value, a user limit could be ignored after moving from a slow screen to a fast one). A Windows "default" refresh rate (0 or 1 Hz) no longer caps at 1 fps: 60 Hz. Firestorm reads the refresh rate of the main screen once (`LLWindowWin32`, `mRefreshRate`); each Aurora window follows its own screen;
  - presentation mode chosen by a single rule (`aurora-render/src/present.rs`): at launch `Mailbox` without sync and `FifoRelaxed` with it, but `Immediate` and `Fifo` after a toggle in the preferences; a session now presents like a launch with the same setting. Selected mode and the surface's modes in the log, `present=` and `screen_hz=` in `perf settings`;
  - diagnostics: `AURORA_PRESENT_MODE=immediate|mailbox|fifo|fifo-relaxed` (docs/TESTING.md); the bug report gives the frame rate limit, the presentation mode and the screen's refresh rate.
