- 🟡 Starting from a SLURL (#676; LLAppViewer::initConfiguration, LLAppViewerWin32::sendURLToOtherInstance, LLViewerWindow::handleDataCopy, LLURLDispatcher, LLCommandHandlerRegistry::dispatch, LLLoginHandler, cmd_line.xml, installer_template.nsi): the startup SLURL (`-url`, `--url` or a bare argument; nothing after it is read, the Legacy Viewer's `last_option`) is the login screen's start location for the next login only, shown first in every start menu (cards and form; the saved choice stays), and the place's details once in the world. A second launch hands its link to the viewer already running through a named pipe of the user's session (`slurl_handoff.rs`; demo mode and `--title` windows have their own) and stops; the window comes to the front. `secondlife:///app/…` commands from outside follow the untrusted rules: throttled ones (profile, group, map, inventory…) one every 5 s with the ThrottledSLURL notice, click-only and blocked ones (chat, search, wear / add / remove folder, balance) refused with the BlockedSLURL notice. `--grid agni|aditi|<uri>`, `--loginuri`, `--login <first> <last> <password>` (logs in at once, usual remember choices). Preferences › Interface › "Open secondlife:// links in Aurora" writes the installer's class for the current Windows user (HKCU, `"<exe>" -url "%1"`), names the program that has the links otherwise, and gives them back when turned off; a published build re-points a registration left on a moved Aurora. Deliberate differences: `app/teleport` from outside opens the place's details instead of being refused (never a teleport without a click in the viewer); a command given at startup runs once in the world (the Legacy Viewer drops it). Validated by the human on 2026-10-21 (link handler on and off, link from a web page to the running viewer and at startup). **To test on Agni:** `--login` with a saved and a new account; a profile or group link from a web page once in the world; a link to a region that does not exist
  - 🟡 Linux (no issue of its own; LLAppViewerLinux::initSLURLHandler and sendURLToOtherInstance, linux_tools/register_secondlifeprotocol.sh and handle_secondlifeprotocol.sh): the same Preferences switch writes a hidden `aurora-viewer-slurl.desktop` (`<exe> -url %u`, the path escaped as the Desktop Entry specification asks, the three schemes) into `$XDG_DATA_HOME/applications` and makes it the `x-scheme-handler/<scheme>` default in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/mimeapps.list`, the rest of the file kept; the handler shown is read in the specification's order (desktop-specific lists first, then `mimeinfo.cache`); turning it off removes our defaults and entry; a published build re-points an entry left on a moved executable. The hand-over goes over the session bus like the Legacy Viewer's (method `GoSLURL(s)`), under Aurora's own name `org.aurora_viewer.AuroraViewer` (`.Demo`, `.T_<title>` for test windows) rather than the Legacy Viewer's shared `com.secondlife.ViewerAppAPIService`; the bus frees the name when the viewer exits, a crash included. Deliberate difference: no shell scripts and no `xdg-mime` / `update-desktop-database` calls, the two files are written directly. Limit: on Wayland the window does not come to the front (winit has no activation token to give). Validated by the contributor on Agni on 2026-10-30 (Hyprland, Wayland): switch on and off (entry and the three defaults written, then removed with the rest of `mimeapps.list` unchanged), a link at startup sets the login start location, links opened while the viewer runs reach it (on the login screen and in the world) without starting a second one. ⬜ Not checked yet: X11 (the window coming to the front) and another desktop (GNOME or KDE). each control active according to the same rights (isParcelModifiableByAgent with the GP_LAND_* group power), changes sent at once (ParcelPropertiesUpdate capability, UDP fallback). **General**: name, ID (RemoteParcelRequest), description, region type, category, owner, group (Choose), deeding to the group (Deed), sale (Sell land: price, buyer, objects, confirmations; Cancel land sale), acquisition, area, traffic (ParcelDwellRequest), Abandon / Reclaim, Buy a pass. **Rules**: estate, owner, covenant text (EstateCovenantRequest then the notecard by asset transfer from the estate), date, resale / subdivision. **Objects**: capacities, return of the objects of the owner / of the group / of others and of an owner in the list (Firestorm's confirmations), auto return, list of owners (ParcelObjectOwnersRequest, online = in our region, FIRE-1292). **Options**: rules of onCommitAny (group ticked automatically with "All", no pushing imposed by the region, scripts cannot be turned off in a damage area), search (128 m²), maturity, category, picture, landing point (Set / Clear / Teleport, FIRE-10043), teleport rules. **Media**: type (widgets from mime_types.xml), home page (MIME type by HEAD request), description, texture, scale, size, loop. **Sound**: music URL with the list of saved streams (FIRE-593, saved in the settings), local sounds, avatar sounds, voice, MOAP. **Access**: public, 18 years old, payment, group, pass, allowed / banned lists (adding through a resident picker: AvatarPickerSearch search, friends, nearby, UUID; Group names by UUIDGroupNameRequest. - 🟡 Teleports between residents like Firestorm, part B1: receiving, network and routing (decided with the human on 2026-10-14; `world/teleport_invites.rs`). Validated in demo by the human on 2026-10-14.
  - A teleport offer (IM_LURE_USER) keeps its entry in the notification centre, Teleport / Decline, with the TeleportOffered sound. It now shows where it leads (FIRE-6786): the lure bucket gives the region and the position (parse_lure_bucket), the region name comes from the world map (asked once with MapBlockRequest when unknown). Its text goes to the sender's transcript (log_to_im). Decline or close sends IM_LURE_DECLINED (lure_callback).
  - A teleport request (IM_TELEPORT_REQUEST) is an entry of the notification centre, "<name> is requesting to be teleported to your location", Yes / No (TeleportRequest). Yes offers a teleport as send_lures does (no text, our location SLURL) and writes the "Teleport offer sent" notice; No sends nothing (teleport_request_callback). Before: it landed in the nearby chat as "Name: text", and was lost without a text.
  - A god lure (IM_GODLIKE_LURE_USER) is accepted at once, without a box (TeleportLureRequest with TELEPORT_FLAGS_VIA_GODLIKE_LURE | DISABLE_CANCEL). Before: ignored.
  - "Reject teleport offers and requests", muted senders and the automatic responses keep their rules (process_improved_im).
  - Deliberate difference: Firestorm shows nothing when our offer is declined or accepted (IM_LURE_DECLINED / IM_LURE_ACCEPTED end in its "unknown dialog" log). Aurora writes a system line, "<name> declined your teleport offer", in the conversation with that resident, or only in their transcript when none is open, instead of the former notification: the sender otherwise never learns the answer.
  - Each offer and request is a pending invitation with its answer (`TeleportInvites`); `World::answer_teleport_invite` answers it and closes its notification, ready for the card of part B2.
  - Demo: `AURORA_DEMO_LURE=offer|request|god|answers|reject`.

A Wayland window cannot know it is minimized, so it never flashes there: Wayland's attention request is an xdg_activation one, and a compositor that grants activations (Hyprland with `misc:focus_on_activate`) switched to the viewer's workspace and focused it on every message.

- ✅ **Script preprocessor: `#include <...>` taken as written** (task `preproc-angle-include`, no issue; validated by the human on the grid on 2026-10-30): the include argument was macro-expanded even in its `<file>` form, so a header defining a folder name as an empty macro (`#define LIB`) turned every later `#include <LIB/file>` into `</file>` and the include was not found. A `"file"` or `<file>` header name is now used as written; only the macro form `#include NAME` is expanded, as the Legacy Viewer's Boost.Wave does (C99 6.10.2; FSLSLPreprocessor, indra/newview/fslslpreproc.cpp). Regression test `header_names_are_not_macro_expanded`.

## Audio and voice

- 🟡 Linux sound through the PulseAudio / PipeWire server (task `linux-pulseaudio-host`, no issue; PR [#1407](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/pull/1407); validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-29: sound heard, output and capture streams in the server, the output reopened on the new default sink both ways): the viewer opened ALSA's `default`, which on a system without `pipewire-alsa` or the Pulse ALSA plugin is the sound card itself, so it bypassed the sound server (no stream in the mixer, the default sink and its effects skipped, the card held). cpal's `pulseaudio` host (a pure-Rust client of the protocol, no system library; PipeWire answers it through `pipewire-pulse`) is now the default on Linux, with ALSA when no server runs: Preferences lists the server's real sinks and sources. Its default buffers are two seconds, so output asks for periods of about 20 ms (40 ms queued, as on Windows; pipewire-pulse rounds them to 1024 frames) and capture for 40 ms fragments (20 ms dropped audio on a short stall, see below). 24-bit sinks and sources (`I24` in cpal) are played and recorded. "Default" follows the server's default sink and source: the host opens a stream on the device index it resolved, so the output and capture threads check the default every 2 s and reopen when it changes, as ALSA's `default` does, and as the Legacy Viewer's voice does (`LLWebRTCImpl::updateDevices`, indra/llwebrtc/llwebrtc.cpp). The PipeWire host was rejected: it links libpipewire and needs libclang to build.
  - ⬜ To verify on the grid (the human logs in): voice on Linux through PipeWire (`pipewire-pulse`): speak for a minute while the viewer is busy (arrival in a busy region), heard without cuts by another resident; switch the default microphone in the desktop while speaking
  - ⬜ later: a capture stall over 40 ms drops microphone audio (voice on the grid not yet tested). cpal's PulseAudio host sets a record stream's `max_length` to its `fragment_size` (`buffer_attr_for_config`), so the server holds one fragment; and its callback thread, unlike the ALSA host's, is not promoted to realtime. Both are cpal's; report upstream, or go back to 20 ms fragments with a larger `max_length` once cpal allows it
  - ⬜ later: Preferences › Sound lists the devices on the UI thread when the page opens; on the PulseAudio host that is two round trips to the server (two client handshakes), which a hung server holds up to 2 s each. Move the listing to a background task
  - ⬜ later: the mixer names the viewer `cpal-pulseaudio-<pid>` and the server cannot restore its volume across runs, until cpal can name the application and its streams (cpal PR #1409, unreleased)

The toggle shortcut, push-to-talk (both modes) and the Conversations microphone are refused there too (`toggle_voice` / `voice_follow_key`). Arriving on such land switches an open microphone off without the toggle sound (`LLWebRTCVoiceClient::leaveChannel(true)`). A call keeps its own channel and is never denied; while the region or parcel is not known yet, the microphone is left as it is. Demo: `AURORA_DEMO_RESTRICTED=1 AURORA_DEMO_TALK=1`; with `AURORA_DEMO_LAND=sound:owner`, the demo simulator now pushes `ParcelVoiceInfo` after a parcel change, as the grid does, so the voice switch of About Land acts on the parcel the avatar stands on.

Every volume slider goes through `widgets::volume_slider` (Preferences › Sound, the volume panel of the top bar, the media controls, a resident's voice row in their menus, the call strip and stage menus). With the option on, the knob moves along the cubic curve of PulseAudio's and ALSA's mixers (gain = position³: −18 dB at the middle, silence at the bottom, exact inverse); a resident's voice (0–200 %) keeps 100 % at the middle, its lower half on the curve. The stored values stay the linear gains of the Legacy Viewer (LLPanelVolumePulldown, LLSpeakerVolumeStorage, which has no such option): turning the option on or off moves the knobs, never the loudness; shown percentages stay the real gain. The import window's sound gain is an upload setting, not a playback volume, and keeps its linear slider. ## To explore

Open-source technologies that could set Aurora apart (human request of 2026-10-16). Not decided: each one needs a feasibility study first (Rust integration, size, cost per frame, licence). All the licences listed fit the GPLv3. Large models (translation, speech) cannot be embedded in the exe: they would be downloaded on demand when the option is turned on.

- ⬜ Noise suppression of the microphone with a neural filter (RNNoise, BSD; or DeepFilterNet, MIT / Apache 2.0): keyboard, fan and room echo removed far better than classic filters, at a small cost. First in the suggested order.
- ⬜ Better levels of detail for meshes, rigged avatars first, with meshoptimizer (MIT): simplification and vertex cache ordering, for more frames per second in crowds. First in the suggested order.
- ⬜ Local translation of nearby chat and IMs with Bergamot / Marian (MPL-2.0, the engine of Firefox Translations): on the PC, no API key, no message sent to an online service; one model of about 20 to 40 MB per language pair.
- ⬜ GPU-ready compressed textures in the cache (Basis Universal, Apache 2.0, or bc7enc, MIT): far less JPEG2000 decoding, faster loading, up to four times less video memory (see also the BC7 line of "Optimisation").
- ⬜ Captions of voice chat with whisper.cpp (MIT): other residents' voices transcribed on the PC, for deaf or hard-of-hearing residents and for muted sound; model of 75 to 150 MB, optional.
- ⬜ Spatial audio with Steam Audio (Apache 2.0): binaural 3D sound, occlusion by walls, room reverberation, for venues and nearby voice.
- 🟡 Ambient occlusion with Intel's XeGTAO (MIT): an option of Preferences › Graphics, see the GTAO line of "Rendering".
- 🟡 Visibility bitmask (Therrien et al., "Screen Space Indirect Lighting with Visibility Bitmask", 2023), after GTAO: a thickness per sample instead of XeGTAO's heuristic (thin objects, hair, railings occlude without darkening what is behind them), then screen-space indirect light from the same horizon search — done as Preferences › Graphics › Indirect light (GTAO), see the GTAO line of "Rendering"
- ⬜ God rays, decided for later by the human on 2026-10-17 (the Legacy Viewer has none):
  - first, screen-space light shafts: a radial blur from the sun's position on screen through the depth (GPU Gems 3, "Volumetric Light Scattering as a Post-Process"), about 0.1 to 0.3 ms, fading out when the sun leaves the frame
  - then possibly froxel volumetric lighting with the shadow cascades (Wronski 2014, Hillaire 2015), about 0.5 to 1.5 ms, to match with the SL sky's haze, water and transparent faces; it would open volumetric fog and projector beams later
- AMD FSR upscaling is already planned in "Rendering" (the upscaler chosen for Aurora).

- ✅ Saved files read by an older build (2026-10-14, validated by the human on 2026-10-14 on the strength of the tests and of a demo run on a settings file from a newer build, with nothing visible to test): a value the build does not understand (a shortcut added later, a new enum variant, a field whose type changed) made the whole `settings.json` fall back to the defaults, and the next save erased the file. `tolerant.rs` reads strictly first, then removes only the value `serde_path_to_error` names (an object entry, a list element; a required field or a fixed tuple climbs to its container) and reads again: unknown fields are ignored, lists keep their valid elements, one log line per value left out (its path, never its value). `settings.json` from a newer version (higher `settings_version`) runs no migration and is written back over the newer file: keys this build does not know stay, values it could not read stay while unchanged here, and the newer version number is kept. Any repaired or unreadable file is first copied to `<name>.newer-backup.json`. Applied to `settings.json`, `login_accounts.json` (shown without the unreadable entries, never rewritten while they are there, as an unreadable catalogue already was), `hud_scales.json` and the skin's `theme.json` / `layout.json`. Raw addresses, panic messages, paths and log lines are never copied.
